Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verses 1–2:

Surat al-Kahf has one hundred and ten verses (215/a). It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Praise be to Allah, who sent down to His servant the Book﴾. Allah praised Himself for His favour upon His creation, and He singled out His Messenger (ﷺ) for mention, because the sending down of the Qur'an to him was a blessing upon him in particular and upon all people in general. ﴿And has not made in it any crookedness﴾; ﴿upright﴾. There is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in it. Its meaning is: He sent down to His servant the Book, upright, and has not made in it any crookedness. "Qayyiman" means: straight. Ibn 'Abbas said: just. Al-Farra' said: "qayyiman" means guardian over all the Books, i.e., confirming them and abrogating their laws (nasikh li-shara'i'iha).

Qatadah said: it is not an inversion; rather the meaning is: He sent down to His servant the Book and did not make in it any crookedness, but He made it upright, and it contains no contradiction, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much contradiction﴾ [al-Nisa': 82].

It was also said: the meaning is that He did not make it created. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: "An Arabic Qur'an, without crookedness" [al-Zumar: 28], that this means: not created.

﴿To warn of a severe punishment﴾, i.e., to warn of a severe punishment ﴿from Him﴾, i.e., from His presence ﴿and to give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a goodly reward﴾, i.e., Paradise.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 3–9:

﴿Remaining therein forever﴾. That is: abiding therein.

﴿And to warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son."﴾

﴿They have no knowledge of it, nor did their fathers﴾. That is: they said it out of ignorance, not out of knowledge. ﴿Grave is the word﴾: that is, great is it in magnitude. ﴿A word﴾ is in the accusative as a tamyiz (specification). It is said that its implied sense is: "How grave is the word, as a word." It is also said that it is from kalimatin, with "min" (from) omitted, so it takes the accusative. ﴿It comes out of their mouths﴾: that is, it emerges from their mouths. ﴿They speak nothing but a lie﴾: that is, what they say is nothing but falsehood.

﴿So perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over them, [if] they do not believe in this message﴾, that is, the Qur'an, ﴿in sorrow﴾: that is, in grief. It is also said: in anger.

﴿Indeed, We have made that which is on the earth an adornment for it﴾. If it is asked: what adornment is there in snakes, scorpions and devils?

It is said: there is adornment in them in the sense that they indicate the oneness of Allah, the Exalted.

Mujahid said: He meant by it men exclusively, for they are the adornment of the earth. It is also said: He meant by them the scholars and the righteous. And it is said: the adornment is by plants, trees and rivers, as He said: ﴿until, when the earth takes on its adornment and is beautified﴾ [Yunus: 24].

﴿That We may test them﴾: that We may examine them, ﴿as to which of them is best in deed﴾: that is, which of them is most righteous in action. It is also said: which of them is most abstinent from the world.

﴿And indeed, We will make that which is on it a barren, bare ground﴾. So "al-sa'id" is the surface of the earth. It is also said: it is dust. "Juruzan" means dry and smooth, producing nothing. It is said: "jarazat al-ard" when its vegetation has been eaten.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or do you think that the companions of the cave and the inscription were among Our signs as a wonder?﴾ means: Did you suppose, O Muhammad, that the companions of the cave and the inscription were among Our signs as a wonder? That is, they are a wonder among Our signs.

It is also said: the meaning is that they are not more wondrous than Our signs, for what I created of the heavens and the earth and what is in them of wonders is more wondrous than them.

"Al-kahf" is the cave in the mountain. They differed concerning "al-raqim." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is a tablet on which were written the names of the companions of the cave and their stories [[addition from "b".]]—and this is the most apparent of the opinions—then they placed it at the entrance of the cave. The tablet was of lead. It is also said: of stone. On this view, "al-raqim" means "al-marqum," that is, "the written," and "al-raqm" is writing.

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that it is the name of the valley in which the companions of the cave were, and on this view it is from "raqmat al-wadi," which is its side.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: it is the name of the town from which the companions of the cave departed.

It is also said: it is the name of the mountain in which the cave is.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 10 (part 1 of 4):

Then Allah mentioned the story of the People of the Cave, saying: ﴿When the youths took refuge in the cave﴾, meaning they went to it. They differed about the reason for their going to the cave [[These are the narrations that the author cites: al-Tabari in his tafsir (15/200-205), al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (5/363-370, 373), al-Qurtubi (10/358-360), and al-Khazin (4/160-165). These narrations, in this detail concerning the departure of the youths, their names, the name of their dog, and so on, are in their entirety transmitted from the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab) who embraced Islam. Some Companions and Successors (Tabi'un) took them from those people and related them because of their strangeness and wonder. Here we set down the words of some verifying scholars and exegetes regarding these narrations, which spare us from commenting on the tafsir at many points. The Hafiz Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (3/76-79): "...Allah the Exalted did not inform us of the location of this cave, nor in which of the lands it lies, since there is no benefit for us in it and no legislative purpose. Some exegetes have strained to mention views on it... Allah knows best in which land of Allah it is. Had there been a religious benefit in it, Allah and His Messenger would have guided us to it... He informed us of its description and did not inform us of its location." After mentioning some views about the dog of the People of the Cave and its color, he said: "They differed about its color in statements that have no outcome, no advantage, no proof, and no need for them. Rather, they are of what is forbidden, for their basis is conjecture about the unseen." He said concerning the names of the youths: "...Concerning their naming with these names and the name of their dog, there is doubt about its authenticity, and Allah knows best, for most of that is transmitted from the People of the Book. Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿So do not argue concerning them except with an apparent argument﴾, meaning an easy and simple matter, for knowing that matter does not entail any great benefit." In al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya (2/115) he said: "Many storytellers (qussas) and exegetes have related about this dog a long account, most of which is transmitted from the Isra'iliyyat, and much of it is false and of no benefit, such as their disagreement about its name and color." The Ustadh Sayyid Qutb said in his book Fi Zilal al-Qur'an (15/2260-2261): "The story of the People of the Cave comes to present a model of faith in believing souls, how they find peace in it, prefer it over the adornments and enjoyments of the earth, and seek refuge in the cave when it becomes hard for them to live among people, and how Allah watches over these believing souls, protects them from trial, and envelops them with mercy. There are various narrations and many sayings about the story; it appeared in some ancient books and in legends in various forms. We stop here at what came in the Qur'an, for it is the sole certain source, and we set aside all the narrations and legends that have crept into the tafsirs without a sound chain, especially since the Noble Qur'an has forbidden seeking rulings from other than the Qur'an concerning it, and disputing about it and arguing conjecturally about the unseen." The Shaykh Muhammad al-Amin al-Shinqiti said in Adwa' al-Bayan (4/20): "Know that the story of the People of the Cave, their names, and in which place of the earth they were, none of that has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) beyond what is in the Qur'an. The exegetes have many Isra'ili reports on it, which we have turned away from mentioning for lack of trust in them." See also: al-Isra'iliyyat wa'l-Mawdu'at by Shaykh Muhammad Abu Shahba, pp. 235-237.]]. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: The People of the Gospel fell into corruption, great sins multiplied among them, and the kings transgressed among them until they worshipped idols and sacrificed to the tyrants (taghut). Yet among them there remained remnants upon the religion of the Messiah, adhering to the worship and monotheism of Allah. Among their kings who did this was a king of the Romans called "Decius" (Diqyanus), who worshipped idols, sacrificed to the tyrants, and killed whoever opposed him. He would descend upon the villages of the Romans, and he would not leave in any town where he alighted anyone except that he tempted them until they worshipped idols and sacrificed to the tyrants, or he killed them. Then he descended upon the city of the People of the Cave, which is "Afsus." When he alighted there, it weighed heavily upon the people of faith, so they hid from him and fled in every direction. When Diqyanus arrived there, he ordered that the people of faith be pursued and gathered for him, and he appointed police (shurta) from among the disbelievers of its people, who followed the people of faith to their places and brought them out to Diqyanus. He would give them the choice between death and worshipping idols and sacrificing to the tyrants. Some of them preferred life, and some refused to worship other than Allah and were killed. When those of firm faith in Allah saw this, they began to surrender themselves to torment and death, and they were killed and cut to pieces. Then the parts of their bodies were hung on the walls of the city on its sides and on each of its gates, until the trial grew severe. When the youths saw this, they grieved greatly. They rose and occupied themselves with prayer, fasting, almsgiving, glorification, and supplication. They were from the nobles of the Romans, and they were eight men. They wept and humbled themselves before Allah and kept saying: "Our Lord, Lord of the heavens and the earth, we shall never call upon any god besides Him. We would have uttered an enormity if we had worshipped other than Him. Remove from Your servants, the believers, this trial, and lift from them this affliction, until they can openly worship You." While they were in this state, having entered a place of prayer (musalla) of theirs, the police caught up with them and found them prostrating on their faces, weeping and humbling themselves before Allah. They said to them: "What has kept you from the king's command? Come along to him." Then they went out and reported their matter to Diqyanus, saying: "You are gathering the people to sacrifice to your gods, and these youths, from your own household, mock you and disobey your command!" When he heard of this, he sent for them and they were brought, their eyes streaming with tears and their faces covered with dust. He said to them: "What has prevented you from witnessing the sacrifice to our gods, which are worshipped on the earth, and from making yourselves an example to the leaders among the people of your city? Choose: either you sacrifice to our gods, or I will kill you." Maksalmina, who was their eldest, said: "Indeed we have a God who fills the heavens and the earth in greatness. We shall never call upon any god besides Him, ever. To Him belong praise, glorification, and exaltation from ourselves, sincerely and forever. Him alone we worship, and from Him we seek deliverance and goodness. As for the tyrants, we shall never worship them, ever. So do with us as you see fit." The companions of Maksalmina said to Diqyanus the same as Maksalmina had said. When they said that, he commanded that the garments they wore, which were of the garments of his dignitaries, be taken off them. Then he said: "I will finish with you and carry out for you what I threatened you with of punishment. What prevents me from hastening that for you is only that I see you as young men whose ages are fresh, so I do not wish to destroy you until I set for you a term in which you may remember and reconsider your minds." Then he commanded that the ornaments of gold and silver that were on them be removed, and then he commanded that they be taken out from his presence.

Diqyanus set out for another city, not their city, near them, for some of his affairs. When the youths saw his departure, they hastened to act before his return, and they feared that when he came to their city he would seek them out [and torment them] [[The words in brackets are omitted in manuscript "B".]]. So they agreed among themselves that each man of them should take some money from his father's house, to give alms from it and to take provision with what remained, then go to a cave near the city on a mountain called Bakhlus, where they would remain and worship Allah, until Diqyanus came, when they would come to him and stand before him, and he would do with them what he willed. When some of them said this to others, each youth went to his father's house, took some money, and gave alms from it. Then they set off with what remained with them, and their dog, which belonged to them, followed them, until they reached that cave and remained in it.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: They passed by a dog, which followed them, and they drove it away. They did this several times, and then the dog said to them: "O people, what do you want from me? Do not fear my side; I love the beloved of Allah. So sleep, and I will guard you."

Ibn Abbas said: They fled by night from Diqyanus, and they were seven. They passed by a shepherd who had a dog, and it followed them on their religion, and the dog of the shepherd followed it. They went out of the town to the cave, which was near the town.

Ibn Ishaq said: They remained in it, having no occupation but prayer, fasting, glorification, magnification, and praise, seeking the Face of Allah. They entrusted their provision to a youth among them called Tamlikha, who used to buy their food from the city secretly. He was one of the strongest and most capable of them. When he entered the city, he would take off the fine clothes he wore and put on garments like those of the poor who beg for food. Then he would take out his silver and go to the city and buy food and drink for them, and he would secretly seek news whether he and his companions had been mentioned in anything. Then he would return to his companions. They remained in this state for as long as they remained. Then Diqyanus came to the city and ordered the notables of its people to sacrifice to the tyrants, and the people of faith were terrified by this. Tamlikha was in the city buying food for his companions. He returned to his companions weeping, with a little food, and informed them that the tyrant had entered the city, and that they had been mentioned and sought along with the notables of the city. They were terrified, fell into prostration, calling upon Allah, humbling themselves before Him, and seeking refuge with Him from trial. Then Tamlikha said to them: "O my brothers, raise your heads and eat, and put your trust in your Lord." They raised their heads, their eyes streaming with tears, and they ate at sunset. Then they sat talking, studying together, and reminding one another. While they were in this state, Allah cast sleep upon their ears in the cave, and their dog was stretching out its forelegs at the entrance of the cave. What befell them befell it too, while they were believers and certain, and their provision was by their heads.

When the next day came, Diqyanus missed them and searched for them but did not find them. He said to some of them: "The matter of these youths who have gone has troubled me. They thought that I was angry with them because of their ignorance of what I had in mind. I would not have borne ill toward them if they had repented and worshipped my gods." The notables of the city said: "You are not worthy of showing mercy to a people who are wicked, rebellious, and disobedient. You had set a term for them, and if they had wished, they would have returned within that term, but they did not repent." When they said this, he became exceedingly angry. Then he sent for their fathers, brought them, and asked them about the youths. He said: "Tell me about your rebellious sons who disobeyed me," and he threatened them with death. They said to him: "As for us, we have not disobeyed you. Why do you kill us over a people who are rebellious, who have taken our wealth and squandered it in the markets of the city, then went off and climbed up a mountain called Bakhlus?" When they told him this, he let them go, and he did not know what to do with the youths. Allah cast into his soul the idea of commanding that the cave be sealed up over them, and Allah wished to honor them and make them a sign for a nation that would succeed them, and to show them that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it, and that Allah will resurrect those in the graves. So Diqyanus commanded that the cave be sealed over them, and he said: "Leave them as they are in the cave, to die of hunger and thirst, and let their cave, which they chose, be their grave." He thought that they were awake and knew what was being done to them, but Allah had taken their souls in a death like sleep, and their dog was stretching out its forelegs at the entrance of the cave. Its state was that which covered them, and they turned from side to side ﴿to the right and to the left﴾.

Then two believing men in the household of King Diqyanus, concealing their faith, one of whom was named Yandarus and the other Runas, agreed to write the story of the youths, their lineages, their names, and their account on a tablet of lead, and to place them in a chest of copper, and to place the chest in the building. They said: "Perhaps Allah will cause a people of believers to come upon these youths before the Day of Resurrection, so that whoever opens the cave may know their account when he reads this book." They did so and built over it. Then Diqyanus remained for as long as he remained, then he died along with his people, and many generations came after him, and kingdoms succeeded kingdoms.

Ubayd ibn Umayr said: The People of the Cave were young men wearing torques (ṭawq) and crowns, with long locks of hair. With them was their hunting dog. They went out to a great festival of theirs, in splendid attire and a grand procession, and they brought out with them the idols they worshipped. God had cast faith into the hearts of the youths, and one of them was the vizier of the king. They believed, but each of them concealed his faith. They said to themselves: "Let us leave from among these people, so that no punishment for their crime befalls us." One youth went out until he reached the shade of a tree and sat down in it. Then another came out, saw him sitting alone, and hoped that he was of the same condition as himself, without either of them revealing it. Then the other came out too, and they gathered in one place. Some of them said to others: "What has brought you together?" Each one hid his faith from his companion for fear for himself. Then they said: "Let each youth go out and be alone with his companion, and then one of them will disclose his secret to the other." They did so, and they found that they were all upon faith. There was a cave in the mountain close to them. Some of them said to the others: ﴿Take refuge in the cave; your Lord will spread for you of His mercy﴾. So they entered the cave with their hunting dog, and they slept for three hundred years and nine more. Their people lost track of them and searched for them, but God obscured their traces and their cave from them. They wrote their names and lineages on a tablet: "So-and-so, so-and-so, and so-and-so, sons of our kings, whom we lost in such-and-such a month, in such-and-such a year, in the kingdom of so-and-so son of so-and-so." They placed the tablet in the king's treasury and said: "This will surely have some significance." That king died, and generation after generation came.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: The disciple (ḥawārī) of Jesus, peace be upon him, came to the city of the People of the Cave and wished to enter it. He was told: "At its gate there is an idol, and no one enters it without prostrating to it." He disliked entering it, so he went to a bathhouse close to the city, where he hired himself out to the bathhouse keeper and worked there. The owner of the bathhouse saw blessing in his bathhouse, and some youths of the city became attached to him. He began to inform them of the news of the heavens and the earth and the news of the Hereafter, until they believed him and affirmed him. He had stipulated with the owner of the bathhouse that the night was his, so that no one would come between him and his Lord, nor between him and prayer. He remained on this arrangement until the son of the king came with a woman and entered the bathhouse with her. The disciple reproached him and said: "You are the son of the king, and you enter with this one?" He felt ashamed and left, but then he returned another time, and the disciple said to him the same thing. He cursed him and rebuked him, and paid no attention to it, until they both entered together and died in the bathhouse. The king came, and it was said to him: "The owner of the bathhouse has killed your son." The owner was sought but could not be found, as he had fled. The king asked: "Who used to keep company with him?" They named the youths, and they were sought. They left the city, and they passed by a companion of theirs who shared their faith, and he went with them, and with him was a dog. Night overtook them and brought them to the cave, and they entered it. They said: "We will stay here until night, then we will rise in the morning, God willing, and you will see your opinion." [In another version: "We will spend the night here tonight."] So God struck their ears [with sleep]. The king went out with his companions searching for them until they found them, and they entered the cave. When a man among them wanted to enter it, he was struck with terror, and none of them could bring himself to enter. One of them said: "Did you not say that if you were able to overpower them you would kill them?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then build up the door of the cave over them, and leave them in it to die of hunger and thirst." He did so.

Wahb said: Time passed after time, after the door of the cave had been sealed up. Then a shepherd was overtaken by rain near the cave, and he said: "If I were to open this cave and bring my sheep into it to shelter from the rain, that would be good." He kept working at it until it was opened, and God returned their spirits to them the next morning when they awoke.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Then there ruled over the people of that land a righteous man called "Baydarus." When he became king, he remained in his kingdom for sixty-eight years. The people divided into factions during his rule: some believed in God and knew that the Hour is true, and some denied it. This grieved the righteous king, and he wept and humbled himself before God, and he was deeply saddened when he saw the people of falsehood increasing and prevailing over the people of truth, and saying: "There is no life but the life of this world, and only the spirits are resurrected, not the bodies." Baydarus sent to those who were thought to be good and who were leaders among the creation. But they went on denying the Hour, until they nearly turned the people away from the truth and from the religion of the disciples. When the righteous king saw this, he entered his house, locked it behind him, dressed in sackcloth, placed ashes beneath himself, and sat upon them. He continued for a time, day and night, humbling himself before God Most High and weeping, saying: "O Lord, You see the disagreement of these people, so send them a sign that will make clear to them the falsity of what they are upon." Then the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful, who dislikes the destruction of His servants, desired to manifest the youths, the People of the Cave, to make their condition known to the people, to make them a sign and a proof against them, so that they might know that the Hour is coming, without doubt. He would answer His righteous servant Baydarus, complete His favor upon him, and gather those believers who had been scattered. So God cast into the heart of a man of that town where the cave was (his name was "Awliyanus") the idea to tear down the structure over the mouth of the cave and use its stones to build a pen for his sheep. He hired two boys, and they began to remove those stones and build that pen, until they had removed what was over the mouth of the cave and opened the door of the cave. God veiled them from people by means of terror. When they opened the door of the cave, God, the Possessor of power and authority, the Giver of life to the dead, permitted the youths to sit within the cave. They sat, joyful, with radiant faces and content hearts. Some of them greeted others, as though they had awakened from the very hour in which they used to wake up in the morning after their night's sleep. Then they stood to pray and prayed as they used to do. Nothing that they would find objectionable was seen in their faces or complexions; they were just as they had been when they fell asleep, and they thought that Decius (Diqyanus) was still seeking them. When they had finished their prayer, they said to Yamlikha, the keeper of their expenses: "Tell us what people were saying about our affair last evening, in the presence of this tyrant?" They supposed that they had slept just as they used to sleep, and it seemed to them that they had slept longer than they usually did. So they asked one another. One of them said to the others: "How long have you been asleep?" They said: "We have slept a day or part of a day." Then they said: "Your Lord knows best how long you have stayed." All of this was of little significance to them. Yamlikha said to them: "You have been sought in the city and not found. Today he wants you brought, so that you may be sacrificed to the idols, or he will kill you. Whatever God wills will then be done." Then Maksalmina said to them: "O my brothers, know that you will meet God, so do not disbelieve after your faith when the enemy of God calls you." 

Then they said to Yamlikha: "Go to the city and listen to what is being said about us there, and what is mentioned in the presence of Decius. Be discreet, let no one perceive you, buy food for us and bring it back, and add to the food we brought, for we have awoken hungry." Yamlikha did as he was accustomed to do. He put on his clothes and took the garments in which he disguised himself, and he took silver coins [from their expenses that were with them, which bore the stamp of Decius; they were like the small quarter-dirhams]. Then Yamlikha set out. When he passed by the door of the cave, he saw the stones removed from the entrance of the cave, and he wondered at it. Then he passed on without concern, until he reached the city gate, moving stealthily. He turned away from the road, fearing that someone from its people would see him and recognize him, and would not realize that Decius and his people had perished three hundred years before. When Yamlikha reached the city gate, he raised his eyes and saw, above the top of the gate, a sign that belongs to the people of faith when faith is openly manifest in them. When he saw it, he was amazed and kept looking at it stealthily. He looked to the right and left, then left that gate and moved to another gate of the city, where he saw the same thing. It began to seem to him that this was not the city he had known. He saw many people, new ones he had never seen before. He kept walking and wondering, and it seemed to him that he was bewildered. Then he returned to the gate by which he had entered, and he kept marveling to himself, saying: "Would that I knew what this is! Yesterday evening the Muslims were concealing this sign and hiding it, but today it is openly displayed. Perhaps I am dreaming?" Then he realized that he was not asleep. He took his cloak and put it on his head, then entered the city and walked in the midst of its marketplace, hearing people swearing by the name of Jesus, son of Mary. This increased his fear, and he saw that he was bewildered. He stood leaning his back against a wall of the city and said to himself: "By God, I do not know what this is! Yesterday evening there was no one on the face of the earth who mentioned Jesus, son of Mary, without being killed. Today I hear them, and everyone mentions the name of Jesus and fears no one." Then he said to himself: "Perhaps this is not the city I know. By God, I know of no city near our city." He stood like one bewildered. Then he met a youth and said to him: "What is the name of this city, young man?" He said: "Its name is 'Afsus.'" Yamlikha said to himself: "Perhaps something has afflicted me, or some matter has taken away my reason. By God, I am right to hasten out of it before I am disgraced there or some evil befalls me and I am destroyed." Then he came to himself and said: "By God, if I had hastened out of the city before anyone noticed me, it would have been more fitting for me."

فَدَنَا مِنَ الَّذِينَ يَبِيعُونَ الطَّعَامَ، فَأَخْرَجَ الْوَرِقَ الَّتِي كَانَتْ مَعَهُ فَأَعْطَاهَا رَجُلًا مِنْهُمْ، فَقَالَ: "بِعْنِي بِهَذِهِ الْوَرِقِ طَعَامًا." فَأَخَذَهَا الرَّجُلُ فَنَظَرَ إِلَى ضَرْبِ الْوَرِقِ وَنَقْشِهَا فَعَجِبَ مِنْهُ، ثُمَّ طَرَحَهَا إِلَى رَجُلٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ فَنَظَرَ إِلَيْهَا، ثُمَّ جَعَلُوا يَتَطَارَحُونَهَا بَيْنَهُمْ مِنْ رَجُلٍ إِلَى رَجُلٍ، يَتَعَجَّبُونَ مِنْهَا. ثُمَّ جَعَلُوا يَتَشَاوَرُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ، وَيَقُولُ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ: "إِنَّ هَذَا أَصَابَ كَنْزًا خَبِيئًا فِي الْأَرْضِ مُنْذُ زَمَانٍ وَدَهْرٍ طَوِيلٍ." فَلَمَّا رَآهُمْ يَمْلِيخَا يَتَشَاوَرُونَ مِنْ أَجْلِهِ، فَرِقَ فَرَقًا شَدِيدًا وَجَعَلَ يَرْتَعِدُ، وَيَظُنُّ أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ فَطِنُوا بِهِ وَعَرَفُوهُ، وَأَنَّهُمْ إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يَذْهَبُوا بِهِ إِلَى مَلِكِهِمْ دِقْيَانُوسَ. وَجَعَلَ أُنَاسٌ آخَرُونَ يَأْتُونَهُ فَيَتَعَرَّفُونَهُ [فَلَا يَعْرِفُونَهُ] [[ساقط من "أ".]]، فَقَالَ لَهُمْ وَهُوَ شَدِيدُ الْفَرَقِ مِنْهُمْ: "افْضُلُوا عَلَيَّ، قَدْ أَخَذْتُمْ وَرِقِي، فَأَمْسِكُوهَا، وَأَمَّا طَعَامُكُمْ فَلَا حَاجَةَ لِي بِهِ." فَقَالُوا لَهُ: "مَنْ أَنْتَ يَا فَتَى وَمَا شَأْنُكَ؟ وَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ وَجَدْتَ كَنْزًا مِنْ كُنُوزِ الْأَوَّلِينَ وَأَنْتَ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تُخْفِيَهُ عَنَّا [[ساقط من "أ".]]! فَانْطَلِقْ مَعَنَا وَأَرِنَا وَشَارِكْنَا فِيهِ نُخْفِ عَلَيْكَ مَا وَجَدْتَ، فَإِنَّكَ إِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ نَأْتِ بِكَ إِلَى السُّلْطَانِ فَنُسَلِّمْكَ إِلَيْهِ فَيَقْتُلْكَ." فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ قَوْلَهُمْ قَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ [[ساقط من "أ".]]: "قَدْ وَقَعْتُ فِي كُلِّ شَيْءٍ كُنْتُ أَحْذَرُ مِنْهُ." فَقَالُوا: "يَا فَتَى، إِنَّكَ وَاللَّهِ لَا تَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ تَكْتُمَ مَا وَجَدْتَ." فَجَعَلَ يَمْلِيخَا لَا يَدْرِي مَا يَقُولُ لَهُمْ، وَلَا مَا يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ، وَفَرِقَ حَتَّى مَا [وَجَدَ مَا] [[ساقط من "أ".]] يُخْبِرُ إِلَيْهِمْ شَيْئًا. فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ لَا يَتَكَلَّمُ، أَخَذُوا كِسَاءَهُ فَطَرَحُوهُ فِي عُنُقِهِ، ثُمَّ جَعَلُوا يَقُودُونَهُ فِي سِكَكِ الْمَدِينَةِ [صَغِيرُهُمْ وَكَبِيرُهُمْ] [[ساقط من "ب".]]، حَتَّى سَمِعَ بِهِ مَنْ فِيهَا [فَسَأَلُوهُ؟ مَا الْخَبَرُ؟] [[ساقط من "أ".]]. فَقِيلَ: "هَذَا رَجُلٌ عِنْدَهُ كَنْزٌ." فَاجْتَمَعَ إِلَيْهِ أَهْلُ الْمَدِينَةِ صَغِيرُهُمْ وَكَبِيرُهُمْ، فَجَعَلُوا يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَيْهِ وَيَقُولُونَ: "وَاللَّهِ مَا هَذَا الْفَتَى مِنْ أَهْلِ هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ، وَمَا رَأَيْنَاهُ فِيهَا قَطُّ، وَمَا نَعْرِفُهُ قَطُّ." فَجَعَلَ يَمْلِيخَا لَا يَدْرِي مَا يَقُولُ لَهُمْ، فَلَمَّا اجْتَمَعَ عَلَيْهِ أَهْلُ الْمَدِينَةِ فَرِقَ فَسَكَتَ فَلَمْ يَتَكَلَّمْ. وَكَانَ مُسْتَيْقِنًا أَنَّ أَبَاهُ وَإِخْوَتَهُ بِالْمَدِينَةِ، وَأَنَّ حَسَبَهُ وَنَسَبَهُ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ، مِنْ عُظَمَاءِ أَهْلِهَا، وَأَنَّهُمْ سَيَأْتُونَهُ إِذَا سَمِعُوا بِهِ. فَبَيْنَا هُوَ قَائِمٌ كَالْحَيْرَانِ يَنْتَظِرُ مَتَى يَأْتِيهِ بَعْضُ أَهْلِهِ فَيُخَلِّصُهُ مِنْ أَيْدِيهِمْ، إِذِ اخْتَطَفُوهُ وَانْطَلَقُوا بِهِ إِلَى رَئِيسَيِ الْمَدِينَةِ وَمُدَبِّرَيْهَا اللَّذَيْنِ يُدَبِّرَانِ أَمْرَهَا، وَهُمَا رَجُلَانِ صَالِحَانِ، اسْمُ أَحَدِهِمَا "أَرْيُوسُ" وَاسْمُ الْآخَرِ "طَنْطَيُوسُ" [[في "أ": أسطيوس.]]. فَلَمَّا انْطُلِقَ بِهِ إِلَيْهِمَا ظَنَّ يَمْلِيخَا أَنَّهُ يُنْطَلَقُ بِهِ إِلَى دِقْيَانُوسَ الْجَبَّارِ، فَجَعَلَ يَلْتَفِتُ يَمِينًا وَشِمَالًا، وَجَعَلَ النَّاسُ يَسْخَرُونَ مِنْهُ كَمَا يَسْخَرُونَ مِنَ الْمَجْنُونِ، وَجَعَلَ يَمْلِيخَا يَبْكِي. ثُمَّ رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ فَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ [[ساقط من "أ".]]: "اللَّهُمَّ إِلَهَ السَّمَاءِ وَإِلَهَ الْأَرْضِ، أَفْرِغِ الْيَوْمَ عَلَيَّ صَبْرًا، وَأَوْلِجْ مَعِيَ رُوحًا مِنْكَ تُؤَيِّدُنِي بِهِ عِنْدَ هَذَا الْجَبَّارِ." وَجَعَلَ يَبْكِي وَيَقُولُ فِي نَفْسِهِ: "فُرِّقَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ إِخْوَتِي، يَا لَيْتَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ مَا لَقِيتُ، وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ فَيَأْتُونِي فَنَقُومُ جَمِيعًا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ هَذَا الْجَبَّارِ، فَإِنَّا كُنَّا تَوَاثَقْنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مَعًا وَلَا نَكْفُرُ بِاللَّهِ وَلَا نُشْرِكُ بِهِ شَيْئًا. فُرِّقَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُمْ، فَلَنْ يَرَوْنِي وَلَنْ أَرَاهُمْ أَبَدًا، وَكُنَّا تَوَاثَقْنَا أَنْ لَا نَفْتَرِقَ فِي حَيَاةٍ وَلَا مَوْتٍ أَبَدًا." يُحَدِّثُ بِهِ نَفْسَهُ يَمْلِيخَا، فِيمَا أَخْبَرَ أَصْحَابَهُ حِينَ رَجَعَ إِلَيْهِمْ، حَتَّى انْتَهَى إِلَى الرَّجُلَيْنِ الصَّالِحَيْنِ "أَرْيُوسُ" وَ"طَنْطَيُوسُ" [[في "أ": أسطيوس.]].

فَلَمَّا رَأَى يَمْلِيخَا أَنَّهُ لَا يُذْهَبُ بِهِ إِلَى دِقْيَانُوسَ أَفَاقَ، وَذَهَبَ [[في "أ": وسكن.]] عَنْهُ الْبُكَاءُ، فَأَخَذَ أَرْيُوسُ [وَطَنْطَيُوسُ] [[في "أ": أسطيوس.]] الْوَرِقَ فَنَظَرَا إِلَيْهَا وَعَجِبَا مِنْهَا. ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ أَحَدُهُمَا: "أَيْنَ الْكَنْزُ الَّذِي وَجَدْتَ يَا فَتَى؟" فَقَالَ يَمْلِيخَا: "مَا وَجَدْتُ كَنْزًا، وَلَكِنَّ هَذَا وَرِقُ آبَائِي، وَنَقْشُ هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ وَضَرْبُهَا، وَلَكِنْ وَاللَّهِ مَا أَدْرِي مَا شَأْنِي، وَمَا أَقُولُ لَكُمْ." فَقَالَ أَحَدُهُمَا: "فَمَنْ أَنْتَ؟" فَقَالَ يَمْلِيخَا: "أَمَّا أَنَا فَكُنْتُ أَرَى أَنِّي مِنْ أَهْلِ هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ." فَقَالُوا: "وَمَنْ أَبُوكَ؟ وَمَنْ يَعْرِفُكَ فِيهَا؟" فَأَنْبَأَهُمْ بِاسْمِ أَبِيهِ، فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا أَحَدًا يَعْرِفُهُ وَلَا أَبَاهُ. فَقَالَ لَهُ أَحَدُهُمَا: "أَنْتَ رَجُلٌ كَذَّابٌ، لَا تُنْبِئُنَا بِالْحَقِّ." فَلَمْ يَدْرِ يَمْلِيخَا مَا يَقُولُ لَهُمْ، غَيْرَ أَنَّهُ نَكَّسَ رَأْسَهُ [وَأَطْرَقَ بَصَرَهُ] [[ساقط من "ب".]] إِلَى الْأَرْضِ. فَقَالَ بَعْضُ مَنْ حَوْلَهُ: "هَذَا رَجُلٌ مَجْنُونٌ." وَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ: "لَيْسَ بِمَجْنُونٍ، وَلَكِنَّهُ يُحَمِّقُ نَفْسَهُ عَمْدًا لِكَيْ يَنْفَلِتَ مِنْكُمْ." فَقَالَ لَهُ أَحَدُهُمَا، وَنَظَرَ إِلَيْهِ نَظَرًا شَدِيدًا: "أَتَظُنُّ أَنَّا نُرْسِلُكَ وَنُصَدِّقُكَ بِأَنَّ هَذَا مَالُ أَبِيكَ، وَنَقْشُ هَذَا الْوَرِقِ وَضَرْبُهَا أكثر من ثلثمائة سَنَةٍ؟ وَإِنَّمَا أَنْتَ غُلَامٌ شَابٌّ! أَتَظُنُّ أَنَّكَ تَأْفِكُنَا وَتَسْخَرُ بِنَا، وَنَحْنُ شُمْطٌ كَمَا تَرَى، وَحَوْلَكَ سُرَاةُ أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ وَوُلَاةُ أَمْرِهَا، وَخَزَائِنُ هَذِهِ الْبَلْدَةِ بِأَيْدِينَا، وَلَيْسَ عِنْدَنَا مِنْ هَذَا الضَّرْبِ دِرْهَمٌ وَلَا دِينَارٌ؟ وَإِنِّي لَأَظُنُّنِي سَآمُرُ بِكَ فَتُعَذَّبُ عَذَابًا شَدِيدًا، ثُمَّ أُوثِقُكَ حَتَّى تَعْتَرِفَ بِهَذَا الْكَنْزِ الَّذِي وَجَدْتَهُ."

فَلَمَّا قَالَ ذَلِكَ، قَالَ لَهُمْ يَمْلِيخَا: "أَنْبِئُونِي عَنْ شَيْءٍ أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَنْهُ، فَإِنْ فَعَلْتُمْ صَدَقْتُكُمْ عَمَّا عِنْدِي." قَالُوا: "سَلْ، لَا نَكْتُمُكَ شَيْئًا." قَالَ لَهُمْ: "مَا فَعَلَ الْمَلِكُ دِقْيَانُوسُ؟" قَالُوا: "لَا نَعْرِفُ الْيَوْمَ عَلَى وَجْهِ الْأَرْضِ مَلِكًا يُسَمَّى دِقْيَانُوسَ، وَلَمْ يَكُنْ إِلَّا مَلِكٌ هَلَكَ مُنْذُ زَمَانٍ وَدَهْرٍ طَوِيلٍ، وَهَلَكَتْ بَعْدَهُ قُرُونٌ كَثِيرَةٌ." فَقَالَ يَمْلِيخَا: "إِنِّي إِذًا لَحَيْرَانُ، وَمَا يُصَدِّقُنِي أَحَدٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ بِمَا أَقُولُ. لَقَدْ كُنَّا فِتْيَةً [عَلَى دِينٍ وَاحِدٍ وَهُوَ الْإِسْلَامُ] [[ساقط من "أ".]]، وَإِنَّ الْمَلِكَ أَكْرَهَنَا عَلَى عِبَادَةِ الْأَوْثَانِ وَالذَّبْحِ لِلطَّوَاغِيتِ، فَهَرَبْنَا مِنْهُ عَشِيَّةَ أَمْسٍ، فَنِمْنَا، فَلَمَّا انْتَبَهْنَا خَرَجْتُ لِأَشْتَرِيَ لَهُمْ طَعَامًا وَأَتَجَسَّسَ الْأَخْبَارَ، فَإِذَا أَنَا كَمَا تَرَوْنَ. فَانْطَلِقُوا مَعِي إِلَى الْكَهْفِ الَّذِي فِي جَبَلِ بَنْجَلُوسَ، أُرِيكُمْ أَصْحَابِي." فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ أَرْيُوسُ مَا يَقُولُ يَمْلِيخَا قَالَ: "يَا قَوْمُ، لَعَلَّ هَذِهِ آيَةٌ مِنْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ جَعَلَهَا اللَّهُ لَكُمْ عَلَى يَدَيْ هَذَا الْفَتَى، فَانْطَلِقُوا بِنَا مَعَهُ يُرِينَا أَصْحَابَهُ."

فَانْطَلَقَ مَعَهُ أَرْيُوسُ وَأَسْطَيُوسُ، وَانْطَلَقَ مَعَهُمْ أَهْلُ الْمَدِينَةِ كَبِيرُهُمْ وَصَغِيرُهُمْ نَحْوَ أَصْحَابِ الْكَهْفِ لِيَنْظُرُوا إِلَيْهِمْ. وَلَمَّا رَأَى الْفِتْيَةُ أَصْحَابُ الْكَهْفِ يَمْلِيخَا قَدِ احْتَبَسَ عَنْهُمْ بِطَعَامِهِمْ وَشَرَابِهِمْ عَنِ الْقَدْرِ الَّذِي كَانَ يَأْتِي بِهِ، ظَنُّوا أَنَّهُ قَدْ أُخِذَ فَذُهِبَ بِهِ إِلَى مَلِكِهِمْ دِقْيَانُوسَ. فَبَيْنَمَا هُمْ يَظُنُّونَ ذَلِكَ وَيَتَخَوَّفُونَهُ، إِذْ سَمِعُوا الْأَصْوَاتَ وَجَلَبَ الْخَيْلِ مُصَعِّدَةً نَحْوَهُمْ، فَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُمْ رُسُلُ الْجَبَّارِ دِقْيَانُوسَ بَعَثَ إِلَيْهِمْ لِيُؤْتَى بِهِمْ، فَقَامُوا إِلَى الصَّلَاةِ، وَسَلَّمَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ، وَأَوْصَى بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضًا، قَالُوا: "انْطَلِقُوا بِنَا نَأْتِ أَخَانَا يَمْلِيخَا، فَإِنَّهُ الْآنَ بَيْنَ يَدَيِ الْجَبَّارِ يَنْتَظِرُ مَتَى نَأْتِيهِ." فَبَيْنَمَا هُمْ يَقُولُونَ ذَلِكَ وَهُمْ جُلُوسٌ بَيْنَ ظَهْرَيِ الْكَهْفِ، لَمْ يَرَوْا إِلَّا أَرْيُوسَ وَأَصْحَابَهُ وُقُوفًا عَلَى بَابِ الْكَهْفِ.

وَسَبَقَهُمْ يَمْلِيخَا فَدَخَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَهُوَ يَبْكِي، فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ يَبْكِي بَكَوْا مَعَهُ، ثُمَّ سَأَلُوهُ عَنْ شَأْنِهِ فَأَخْبَرَهُمْ وَقَصَّ عَلَيْهِمُ النَّبَأَ كُلَّهُ. فَعَرَفُوا عِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا نِيَامًا بِأَمْرِ اللَّهِ ذَلِكَ الزَّمَانَ كُلَّهُ، بِأَمْرِ اللَّهِ، وَإِنَّمَا أُوقِظُوا لِيَكُونُوا آيَةً لِلنَّاسِ، وَتَصْدِيقًا لِلْبَعْثِ، وَلِيَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ السَّاعَةَ آتِيَةٌ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهَا.

ثُمَّ دَخَلَ عَلَى أَثَرِ يَمْلِيخَا أَرْيُوسُ، فَرَأَى تَابُوتًا مِنْ نُحَاسٍ مَخْتُومًا بِخَاتَمٍ مِنْ فِضَّةٍ، فَقَامَ بِبَابِ الْكَهْفِ، ثُمَّ دَعَا رَجُلًا مِنْ عُظَمَاءِ أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ، فَفُتِحَ التَّابُوتَ عِنْدَهُمْ [[ساقط من "أ".]]، فَوَجَدُوا فِيهِ لَوْحَيْنِ مِنْ رَصَاصٍ مَكْتُوبًا فِيهِمَا: "أَنَّ مَكْسِلْمِينَا وَمَخْشِلْمِينَا وَيَمْلِيخَا وَمَرْطُونِسْ وَكَشْطُونِسْ وَيَبْرُونِسْ وَدِيمُوسُ وَبَطْيُوسُ وَحَالُوشُ، كَانُوا فَتْيَةً هَرَبُوا مِنْ مَلِكِهِمْ دِقْيَانُوسَ الْجَبَّارِ مَخَافَةَ أَنْ يَفْتِنَهُمْ عَنْ دِينِهِمْ، فَدَخَلُوا هَذَا الْكَهْفَ. فَلَمَّا أُخْبِرَ بِمَكَانِهِمْ أَمَرَ بِالْكَهْفِ فَسُدَّ عَلَيْهِمْ بِالْحِجَارَةِ، وَإِنَّا كَتَبْنَا شَأْنَهُمْ وَخَبَرَهُمْ لِيَعْلَمَهُ مَنْ بَعْدَهُمْ إِنْ عَثَرَ عَلَيْهِمْ."

فَلَمَّا قَرَأُوهُ وَعَجِبُوا وَحَمِدُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي أَرَاهُمْ آيَةَ الْبَعْثِ فِيهِمْ، ثُمَّ رَفَعُوا أَصْوَاتَهُمْ بِحَمْدِ اللَّهِ وَتَسْبِيحِهِ، ثُمَّ دَخَلُوا عَلَى الْفِتْيَةِ إِلَى الْكَهْفِ، فَوَجَدُوهُمْ جُلُوسًا بَيْنَ ظهرانيهم، مُشْرِقَةً وُجُوهُهُمْ، لَمْ تَبْلَ ثِيَابُهُمْ. فَخَرَّ أَرْيُوسُ وَأَصْحَابُهُ سُجُودًا، وَحَمِدُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي أَرَاهُمْ آيَةً مِنْ آيَاتِهِ. ثُمَّ كَلَّمَ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضًا، وَأَنْبَأَهُمُ الْفِتْيَةُ عَنِ الَّذِي لَقُوا مِنْ مَلِكِهِمْ دِقْيَانُوسَ [مِنْ إِكْرَاهِهِمْ عَلَى عِبَادَةِ الْأَوْثَانِ وَالذَّبْحِ لِلطَّوَاغِيتِ، وَإِخْفَاءِ إِيمَانِهِمْ عَنْهُ، وَهَرَبِهِمْ إِلَى الْكَهْفِ] [[ما بين القوسين ساقط من "ب". / ٢ ٢١٦ / ب / ٢.]].

ثُمَّ إِنَّ أَرْيُوسَ وَأَصْحَابَهُ بَعَثُوا بَرِيدًا إِلَى مَلِكِهِمُ الصَّالِحِ بَيْدَرُوسَ: "أَنْ عَجِّلْ إِلَيْنَا، لَعَلَّكَ تَنْظُرُ إِلَى آيَةٍ مِنْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ جَعَلَهَا اللَّهُ فِي مُلْكِكَ، وَجَعَلَهَا آيَةً لِلْعَالَمِينَ، لِتَكُونَ لَهُمْ نُورًا وَضِيَاءً وَتَصْدِيقًا لِلْبَعْثِ. فَاعْجَلْ إِلَى فِتْيَةٍ بَعَثَهُمُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ، وَقَدْ كَانَ تَوَفَّاهُمْ مُنْذُ أكثر من ثلثمائة سَنَةٍ." فَلَمَّا أَتَى الْمَلِكَ الْخَبَرُ رَجَعَ إِلَيْهِ عَقْلُهُ، وَذَهَبَ هَمُّهُ، فَقَالَ: "أَحْمَدُكَ اللَّهَ رَبَّ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ، وَأَعْبُدُكَ وَأُسَبِّحُ لَكَ، تَطَوَّلْتَ عَلَيَّ وَرَحِمْتَنِي، فَلَمْ تُطْفِئِ النُّورَ الَّذِي كُنْتَ جَعَلْتَهُ لِآبَائِي لِلْعَبْدِ الصَّالِحِ أَسْطَنْطَيْنُوسَ الْمَلِكِ."

فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَ بِهِ أَهْلَ الْمَدِينَةِ رَكِبُوا إِلَيْهِ وَسَارُوا مَعَهُ حَتَّى أَتَوْا مَدِينَةَ أَفْسُوسَ، فَتَلَقَّاهُمْ أَهْلُ الْمَدِينَةِ وَسَارُوا مَعَهُ حَتَّى صَعِدُوا نَحْوَ الْكَهْفِ. فَلَمَّا رَأَى الْفِتْيَةُ بَيْدَرُوسَ فَرِحُوا بِهِ وَخَرُّوا سُجَّدًا عَلَى وُجُوهِهِمْ، وَقَامَ بَيْدَرُوسُ فَاعْتَنَقَهُمْ وَبَكَى، وَهُمْ جُلُوسٌ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ يُسَبِّحُونَ اللَّهَ وَيَحْمَدُونَهُ. ثُمَّ قَالَ الْفِتْيَةُ لِبَيْدَرُوسَ: "نَسْتَوْدِعُكَ اللَّهَ [إِيمَانَكَ وَخَوَاتِيمَ أَعْمَالِكَ] [[ساقط من "ب".]] وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ، حَفِظَكَ اللَّهُ وَحَفِظَ مُلْكَكَ، وَنُعِيذُكَ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ شَرِّ الْإِنْسِ وَالْجِنِّ." فَبَيْنَمَا الْمَلِكُ قَائِمٌ إِذْ رَجَعُوا إِلَى مَضَاجِعِهِمْ فَنَامُوا، وَتَوَفَّى اللَّهُ تَعَالَى أَنْفُسَهُمْ. وَقَامَ الْمَلِكُ إِلَيْهِمْ فَجَعَلَ ثِيَابَهُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ، وَأَمَرَ أَنْ يُجْعَلَ كُلُّ رَجُلٍ مِنْهُمْ فِي تَابُوتٍ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ. فَلَمَّا أَمْسَى وَنَامَ أَتَوْهُ فِي الْمَنَامِ، فَقَالُوا لَهُ: "إِنَّنَا لَمْ نُخْلَقْ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ وَلَا مِنْ فِضَّةٍ، وَلَكِنَّا خُلِقْنَا مِنْ تُرَابٍ وَإِلَى التُّرَابِ نَصِيرُ، فَاتْرُكْنَا كَمَا كُنَّا فِي الْكَهْفِ عَلَى التُّرَابِ حَتَّى يَبْعَثَنَا اللَّهُ مِنْهُ." فَأَمَرَ الْمَلِكُ حِينَئِذٍ بِتَابُوتٍ مِنْ سَاجٍ فَجُعِلُوا فِيهِ، وَحَجَبَهُمُ اللَّهُ حِينَ خَرَجُوا مِنْ عِنْدِهِمْ بِالرُّعْبِ، فَلَمْ يَقْدِرْ أَحَدٌ عَلَى أَنْ يَدْخُلَ عَلَيْهِمْ. فَأَمَرَ الْمَلِكُ فَجُعِلَ عَلَى بَابِ الْكَهْفِ مَسْجِدًا يُصَلَّى فِيهِ، وَجَعَلَ لَهُمْ عِيدًا عَظِيمًا، وَأَمَرَ أَنْ يُؤْتَى كُلَّ سَنَةٍ.

It is said: when Yamlikha was brought to the righteous king, the king said to him, "Who are you?" He said, "I am a man from the people of this city," and he mentioned that he had left yesterday or a few days ago, and he mentioned his home and people whom no one recognized. The king had heard that a group of youths had disappeared in the former era, and that their names were written on a tablet in the treasury. So he called for the tablet and looked at their names, and behold, he was one of those people. He also mentioned the names of the others, and Yamlikha said, "They are my companions." When the king heard that, he rode out with those of his people who were with him. When they reached the mouth of the cave, Yamlikha said, "Leave me until I enter upon my companions and give them good news, for if they see you with me they will be frightened." So he entered and gave them good news, and God took their souls and blinded their traces, so that they were not guided to them. This is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic:

﴿When the youths took refuge in the cave﴾, meaning: they went to the cave. It is said: "So-and-so took refuge (awa) at such-and-such a place," meaning he made it his dwelling. The cave is a grotto in the mountain of Banjlus, and the name of the cave is "Khayram" [[See what preceded on p. (145), footnote (2) of the same surah.]].

﴿So they said: "Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself"﴾. The meaning of mercy here is guidance in religion. It is also said: it means provision. ﴿And prepare for us﴾, make easy for us, ﴿from our affair, right guidance﴾, meaning: whatever is sought of Your pleasure and whatever contains our rectitude. Ibn Abbas said: "Rashadan" means a way out of the cave in safety.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verses 11–12:

﴿So We struck upon their ears﴾ meaning: We made them sleep and cast sleep upon them. It is also said: its meaning is that We prevented sounds from reaching their hearing, for a sleeper, when he hears a sound, wakes up. ﴿in the cave for a number of years﴾ meaning: We made them sleep for a counted number of years. Mentioning the number is for emphasis. It is also said: mentioning it indicates abundance, for a small amount is not usually counted.

﴿Then We raised them up﴾, meaning from their sleep, ﴿that We might know﴾ meaning: knowledge of witnessing (ʿilm al-mushāhadah), ﴿which of the two parties﴾ meaning which of the two groups ﴿was more accurate in computing the time they had stayed﴾. This is because the people of the town disputed about the length of their stay in the cave. The scholars differed concerning His words "aḥṣā li-mā labithū" (more accurate in computing what they had stayed): aḥfaẓu (more mindful) of what they remained in their cave asleep, amadan (a term), meaning a limit. Mujahid said: ʿadadan (a number), and its accusative form is by way of explanation (tafsir).

Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on Surah 18, verses 13–16:

﴿We relate to you﴾ [i.e., We recite to you] [[Omitted from manuscript "A".]] ﴿their story﴾, the account of the People of the Cave, ﴿in truth﴾, with sincerity. ﴿Indeed, they were young men﴾, youths, ﴿who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance﴾, in faith and insight.

﴿And We fortified﴾, i.e., strengthened, ﴿their hearts﴾ with patience and steadfastness, and We empowered them with the light of faith, so that they endured abandoning the homeland of their people and leaving behind what they had of honour and comfortable living, and they fled with their religion to the cave. ﴿When they stood up﴾ before Diqyanus (Decius) when he rebuked them for abandoning the worship of the idol, ﴿and said: "Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We shall never call upon any god besides Him."﴾ They said this because their people worshipped idols. ﴿Certainly we would have uttered an enormity if we did so﴾, meaning: if we called upon other than Allah, we would have uttered an enormity. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Injustice." Qatadah said: "Falsehood." The root of *shatat* and *ishtat* is exceeding the proper measure and going to excess.

﴿These, our people﴾, meaning the people of their land, ﴿have taken besides Him gods﴾, i.e., besides Allah, ﴿gods﴾, meaning idols, which they worship. ﴿Why do they not bring for them﴾, i.e., for their worship, ﴿a clear authority﴾, a manifest proof that clarifies and makes evident that idols do not deserve worship besides Allah? ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah?﴾, claiming that He has a partner and a son.

Then some of them said to others: ﴿And when you have withdrawn from them﴾, meaning their people, ﴿and what they worship, except Allah﴾. Ibn Mas'ud recited "and what they worship besides Allah." As for the well-known reading, its meaning is: they used to worship Allah and worship the idols alongside Him, so [the youths] said: "And when you have withdrawn from them and all that they worship except Allah, [then] you have not withdrawn from their worship [of Him]." ﴿Then take refuge in the cave﴾, i.e., betake yourselves to it. ﴿Your Lord will spread for you of His mercy and will prepare for you﴾, i.e., will make easy for you, ﴿from your affair, a means of ease﴾, meaning that which will return to you as ease and comfort. Abu Ja'far, Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read *mirfaqan* with a fatha on the *mim* and a kasra on the *fa'*; the others read it with a kasra on the *mim* and a fatha on the *fa'*. Their meanings are one and the same: it is that by which a person is supported and made comfortable.

﴿And We fortified﴾, i.e., strengthened, ﴿their hearts﴾ with patience and steadfastness, and We empowered them with the light of faith, so that they endured abandoning the homeland of their people and leaving behind what they had of honour and comfortable living, and they fled with their religion to the cave. ﴿When they stood up﴾ before Diqyanus (Decius) when he rebuked them for abandoning the worship of the idol, ﴿and said: "Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We shall never call upon any god besides Him."﴾ They said this because their people worshipped idols. ﴿Certainly we would have uttered an enormity if we did so﴾, meaning: if we called upon other than Allah, we would have uttered an enormity. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Injustice." Qatadah said: "Falsehood." The root of *shatat* and *ishtat* is exceeding the proper measure and going to excess.

﴿These, our people﴾, meaning the people of their land, ﴿have taken besides Him gods﴾, i.e., besides Allah, ﴿gods﴾, meaning idols, which they worship. ﴿Why do they not bring for them﴾, i.e., for their worship, ﴿a clear authority﴾, a manifest proof that clarifies and makes evident that idols do not deserve worship besides Allah? ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah?﴾, claiming that He has a partner and a son.

Then some of them said to others: ﴿And when you have withdrawn from them﴾, meaning their people, ﴿and what they worship, except Allah﴾. Ibn Mas'ud recited "and what they worship besides Allah." As for the well-known reading, its meaning is: they used to worship Allah and worship the idols alongside Him, so [the youths] said: "And when you have withdrawn from them and all that they worship except Allah, [then] you have not withdrawn from their worship [of Him]." ﴿Then take refuge in the cave﴾, i.e., betake yourselves to it. ﴿Your Lord will spread for you of His mercy and will prepare for you﴾, i.e., will make easy for you, ﴿from your affair, a means of ease﴾, meaning that which will return to you as ease and comfort. Abu Ja'far, Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read *mirfaqan* with a fatha on the *mim* and a kasra on the *fa'*; the others read it with a kasra on the *mim* and a fatha on the *fa'*. Their meanings are one and the same: it is that by which a person is supported and made comfortable.

The Prophet's saying "Allah has been used"... (translation follows)

**Allah's words: ﴿And you see the sun, when it rises, inclining away from their cave to the right﴾**

Ibn 'Amir and Ya'qub read *tazawwaru* (تَزْوَرُّ) with a sukun on the zay and a shaddah on the ra', on the pattern of *tahmarru* (تَحْمَرُّ). The people of Kufa read it with a light fatha on the zay and an alif after it. The others read it with a shaddah on the zay. All these readings have one meaning, namely: it inclines and turns away. ﴿away from their cave to the right﴾ means toward the right side. ﴿And when it sets, it passes them by on the left﴾ means it leaves them and turns away from them. ﴿on the left﴾: the root of *qarḍ* (القَرْض) is cutting. ﴿and they were in a spacious place within it﴾ means in a wide part of the cave. Its plural is *fajawat*. Ibn Qutaybah said: Their cave faced the Banat Na'sh (the stars of the Big Dipper), so the sun did not fall on it at sunrise, nor at sunset, nor in between. He said: Allah chose for them a resting place in a hollow where the sun does not reach them, so that its heat does not harm them or change their complexions, while they are in a spacious place where the cool breeze and its gentle air reach them, and which removes from them the distress and sorrow of the cave.

Some scholars said: This view is mistaken. The cave did face the Banat Na'sh, so the sun did not fall upon them, but Allah turned the sun away from them by His power and placed a barrier between it and them. Do you not see that He said:

﴿That is among the signs of Allah﴾, that is, among the wonders of Allah's craftsmanship and the proofs of His power by which one should take heed. ﴿Whom Allah guides is the one who is rightly guided, and whom He leaves astray﴾, that is, whom Allah leaves astray and does not guide, ﴿you will not find for him any protector﴾, any helper, ﴿or guide﴾.

**Allah's words: ﴿And you would think them awake, while they were asleep﴾**

That is, alert. *Ayqaz* (أَيْقَاظًا) is the plural of *yaqiz* and *yaqud*. ﴿while they were asleep﴾ means sleeping, the plural of *raqid*, like *qa'id* and *qu'ud*. Their state appeared like that of the waking because their eyes were open, they breathed, and they did not speak.

**﴿And We turned them to the right and to the left﴾**

Once to the right side and once to the left side. Ibn 'Abbas said: They were turned from side to side once a year, so that the earth would not consume their flesh. It was also said that the Day of 'Ashura was the day of their turning. Abu Hurayrah said: They had two turnings each year.

**﴿And their dog, stretching out its two forelegs at the threshold﴾**

Most of the people of tafsir (exegesis) hold that it was of the species of dogs.

It was narrated from Ibn Jurayj that it was a lion, and the lion was called a dog. The Prophet (ﷺ) invoked against 'Utbah ibn Abi Lahab, saying: "O Allah, set upon him one of Your dogs." Then a lion mauled him. (Al-Hakim authenticated it in *al-Mustadrak*, and al-Dhahabi agreed. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar graded it *hasan* in *Fath al-Bari*, and he also attributed it to al-Bayhaqi in *al-Dala'il*. See *al-Kafi al-Shaf*, p. 160.)

The first view is more sound.

Ibn 'Abbas said: It was a white-faced dog (*aghharr*). It is also narrated from him: it was above the *qalati* and below the *kurdi*. (*Al-Qalati* is a Chinese dog.)

Muqatil said: It was yellow. Al-Qurazi said: The intensity of its yellowness verged on red. Al-Kalbi said: Its color was like *khalanj* (a reddish-brown wood). It was also said: its color was like that of the stone.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Its name was Qitmir. It is narrated from 'Ali that its name was Rayyan. Al-Awza'i said: Bitur. Al-Suddi said: Tawr. Ka'b said: Sahilah. (See the note (2), p. 145 of this surah.)

Khalid ibn Ma'dan said: There is no animal in Paradise except the dog of the People of the Cave and the donkey of Bal'am.

As for ﴿at the threshold (al-wasid)﴾: Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: *al-Wasid* is the courtyard of the cave. 'Ata' said: *al-Wasid* is the threshold of the door. Al-Suddi said: *al-Wasid* is the door, and this is also a narration of 'Ikrimah from Ibn 'Abbas.

If it is asked: The cave had no door or threshold?

It is answered: It means the place of the door and the threshold. The dog stretched out its forelegs and placed its face towards them.

Al-Suddi said: When the People of the Cave turned, the dog turned with them. When they turned to the right, the dog would bend its right ear and lie on it. When they turned to the left, it would bend its left ear and lie on it.

**﴿If you had looked upon them, O Muhammad, you would have turned away from them in flight﴾**

Because of the awe with which Allah had clothed them, so that no one could approach them until the Book reached its term, and then Allah would awaken them from their sleep. ﴿And you would have been filled with terror from them﴾, that is, fear. The people of the Hijaz read *la-mulli'ta* with a shaddah on the lam, and the others read it with a light lam.

They differed about what the terror was caused by. It was said: by the loneliness of the place.

Al-Kalbi said: Because their eyes were open, like one who is awake and about to speak, while they were asleep.

It was also said: because of the abundance of their hair, the length of their nails, and their being turned without any sense or perception.

It was also said: Allah prevented anyone from seeing them by means of terror.

It is narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: We fought with Mu'awiyah towards the Byzantines, and we passed by the cave in which were the People of the Cave. Mu'awiyah said: If only it were uncovered for us regarding these people, so that we could look at them. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them) said: Someone better than you was prevented from that. He said: ﴿If you had looked upon them, you would have turned away from them in flight.﴾ So Mu'awiyah sent some men and said: Go and look. When they entered the cave, Allah sent a wind against them, and it drove them out. (Al-Tha'labi mentioned it. See the tafsir of al-Qurtubi, 10/389.)

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 19:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And thus We raised them up﴾, meaning: just as We put them to sleep in the cave and preserved their bodies from decay over the length of time, so likewise [[Omitted from manuscript "a".]] We raised them from that sleep, which resembles death. ﴿That they might question one another﴾, meaning that some of them would ask others. The lam here is the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah), because they were not raised up for the purpose of questioning.

﴿A speaker among them said﴾, and he was their leader, Maksilmina, ﴿"How long have you remained?"﴾ in your sleep? They were surprised at the length of their sleep. It is said that what had passed of the prayers they had missed troubled them, and so they said this.

﴿They said, "We have remained a day"﴾. The reason is that they had entered the cave in the early morning (ghudwah), and when they awoke in the evening (‘ashiyyah) they said, "We have remained a day." Then they looked, and some of the sun's light remained, so they said: ﴿"Or part of a day."﴾ When they looked at the length of their hair and nails, they knew that they had remained longer than a day.

﴿They said, "Your Lord knows best how long you have remained."﴾ It is also said that when their leader Maklasilmina heard the disagreement among them, he said: "Leave off the disagreement. Your Lord knows best how long you have remained." ﴿So send one of you with this silver of yours﴾, meaning Yamlikha.

Abu 'Amr, Hamzah and Abu Bakr recited "biwarqikum" with the r sukun (bi-warqikum); the rest recited it with a kasrah on the r. Their meaning is the same, and it refers to silver, whether minted or unminted.

﴿To the city﴾. It is said that it is Tarsus, and its name in the pre-Islamic period was Afsus, and in Islam they named it Tarsus.

﴿Then let him look to see which is the purest food﴾, meaning: the most lawful food, so that it is not from usurpation or from a forbidden cause. It is said that they ordered him to seek the slaughter of a believer and not of one who slaughters for other than God. There were believers among them who concealed their faith. Al-Dahhak said: "the best food." Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "the finest food." 'Ikrimah said: "the most abundant." The root of zakah is increase. It is also said: "the cheapest food."

﴿Let him bring you provision from it﴾, meaning: sustenance and food that you may eat. ﴿And let him be gentle﴾, meaning: let him be gentle and considerate on the road and in the city, and let him be discreet and secretive. ﴿And let him not make anyone aware of you﴾, meaning: let him not inform anyone among the people about you.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 20–21:

﴿Indeed, if they gain the upper hand over you﴾, meaning: if they come to know of your whereabouts, ﴿they will stone you﴾. Ibn Jurayj said: they will revile you and harm you with words. It is also said: they will kill you. It is also said: it was among their customs to kill by stoning, and that is the most wicked form of killing. It is also said: they will beat you. ﴿Or they will return you to their religion﴾, meaning: to disbelief. ﴿And then you will never succeed, ever﴾, if you return to it.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And thus We caused them to be found﴾, meaning: We let them be discovered (atla'na) ﴿by them﴾. It is said: "I came upon (ʿathartu) a thing" when you became aware of it, and "I caused another to come upon it" (a'thartu ghayri), meaning: I informed him of it. ﴿So that they might know that the promise of God is true﴾, meaning the people of Baydarus (Baydarus) who denied the Resurrection, ﴿and that the Hour—there is no doubt about it—﴾ when ﴿they disputed among themselves about their affair﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: they disputed concerning the building. The Muslims said: "We will build a mosque over them, where people may pray, because they are upon our religion." And the polytheists said: "We will build over them a structure, because they are of our lineage."

ʿIkrimah said: they disputed about the Resurrection. The Muslims said: the Resurrection is for the bodies and the souls together. And a people said: it is for the souls without the bodies. So God, Exalted is He, raised them up and showed them that the Resurrection is for both the bodies and the souls.

It is also said: they disputed about the length of their sleep. And it is said: about their number.

﴿So they said: "Build over them a structure; their Lord knows best about them."﴾ ﴿Those who prevailed over their affair said: "We will surely take over them a place of worship."﴾ Those who prevailed were King Baydarus and his companions.

The Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 22:

﴿They will say: "They were three, the fourth of them being their dog."﴾ It is narrated that al-Sayyid and al-Aqib and their companions, who were Christians of the people of Najran, were with the Prophet ﷺ, and the mention of the Companions of the Cave came up. Al-Sayyid, who was a Ya'qubi, said: "They were three, the fourth of them being their dog." Al-Aqib, who was a Nestorian, said: "They were five, the sixth of them being their dog." The Muslims said: "They were seven, the eighth of them being their dog." So Allah confirmed the word of the Muslims after recounting the word of the Christians, saying: ﴿They will say: "They were three, the fourth of them being their dog." And they will say: "They were five, the sixth of them being their dog," guessing at the unseen.﴾ [See: Zad al-Masir: 5/124; al-Qurtubi: 10/382.] That is, by conjecture and guesswork without certainty. He did not say this concerning the seven, so He said: ﴿And they will say﴾, meaning the Muslims: ﴿"They were seven, and the eighth of them being their dog."﴾

They differed concerning the waw (and) in His words ﴿and the eighth of them﴾. It was said: omitting it and mentioning it are the same.

It was said: it is the waw of judgment and affirmation (waw al-hukm wa al-tahqiq), as if He related their disagreement, and the speech was complete at His words "and they will say: seven," and then He affirmed this statement with His words ﴿and the eighth of them being their dog﴾, and the eighth cannot be except after the seventh.

It was said: this is the waw of the eight (waw al-thamaniyah), because the Arabs count, saying: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, and eight, since the complete number for them was seven, just as for us today the complete number is ten. A parallel to this is His saying, exalted is He, [See: Zad al-Masir: 5/125; al-Qurtubi: 10/382-383.] "The repentant, the worshippers, the praisers..." up to His words "and those who forbid evil" [al-Tawbah: 112], and He said concerning the wives of the Prophet ﷺ: "It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you, submissive, faithful, obedient, repentant, worshipping, fasting, previously married and virgins" [al-Tahrim: 5].

﴿Say: "My Lord knows best their number."﴾ That is, their count. ﴿None knows them except a few﴾, that is, except a few of the people. Ibn Abbas said: "I am among the few; they were seven."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: "They were eight," reading ﴿and the eighth of them being their dog﴾, meaning their guardian. The correct view is the first.

It is narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: "They were Maksilmina, Yamlikha, Marutunus, Baynunus, Sarinunus, Dhu Nawanis, Kashfaytatunus, and the shepherd, and the dog was Qitmir." [See the earlier note on p. 145. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/337; Zad al-Masir: 5/127; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/72-73.]

﴿So do not argue concerning them﴾, that is, do not dispute with them and do not speak about their number and their condition ﴿except with an apparent argument﴾, that is, only according to the apparent content of what We have related to you. He means: what I have related to you is sufficient for you, so do not add to it, and stop at it. ﴿And do not seek a ruling concerning them from among them﴾, from the People of the Book ﴿anyone﴾, that is, do not return to their statements after We have informed you.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on surah 18, verses 23–24:

﴿And never say of anything, "I will surely do that tomorrow," without adding, "If Allah wills."﴾ That is, when you have resolved to do something tomorrow, do not say, "I will do it tomorrow," until you say, "If Allah wills" (*in shaa' Allah*). The reason is that the people of Makkah asked him about the soul (*ruh*), about the People of the Cave, and about Dhu al-Qarnayn. He said, "I will inform you tomorrow," and he did not say, "If Allah wills." So the revelation was delayed for several days, and then this verse was revealed.

﴿And remember your Lord when you forget﴾. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and al-Hasan said: its meaning is, when you forget the exception (*istithna'*) and then remember, then make the exception.

Ibn Abbas permitted a disconnected exception (*al-istithna' al-munqati'*), even if it was a year later. Al-Hasan permitted it as long as one remains in the same gathering. Some permitted it if the time is near, but if it is distant, it is not valid. A group did not permit an exception unless it is connected to the speech.

[Al-Tabari said in his *tafsir* (exegesis): (5/229–230): "The more correct of the two opinions regarding this is the view of the one who said: its meaning is, 'Remember your Lord when you have left off mentioning Him,' because one of the meanings of *nisyan* (forgetting) in the Arabic language is *tark* (leaving off). If someone says: Is it permissible for a man to make an exception in his oath if the meaning of the speech is what you mentioned, after a period from the state of his oath? It is said: Rather, the correct view is that he should make the exception, even after breaking his oath, by saying, 'If Allah wills,' so that by his saying that he is freed from what Allah has obligated him in this verse, and the burden is removed from him by his leaving off what he was commanded to say. As for the expiation (*kaffarah*), it does not fall from him in any way unless his exception was joined to his oath." Then he explained the view of Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, and the view of the one who said that he may make the exception as long as he is in his gathering, saying: "Their meaning in this is similar to our meaning, that it is permissible for him even after ten years, and that his exception and saying 'If Allah wills' after a period from the state of his oath removes from him the burden that would have been binding on him had he not said it. As for the expiation, it is binding on him by breaking the oath in every case, unless his exception was joined to the oath. This is because we know of no one among those who say the exception is permissible after a period who claims that it removes the expiation if he breaks his oath. In this is the clearest proof for the correctness of what we have said..." This is also what Ibn Kathir preferred (3/80).

Al-Jassas said in *Ahkam al-Qur'an* (5/41–42): "This kind of exception is used to remove the ruling of the speech, so that its existence and non-existence are equal. This is because Allah, the Exalted, enjoined the exception with the will of Allah, so that he does not become a liar in his oath. This indicates that its ruling is what we have described. It is also indicated by the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, relating from Musa, peace be upon him: ﴿You will find me, if Allah wills, patient﴾. He was not patient, and he was not a liar, because of the presence of the exception in his speech. This shows that its meaning is what we have described, its entry into the speech to remove its ruling. Therefore, its ruling must not differ whether it enters an oath, or the pronouncement of divorce, or manumission..." Then he preferred that the exception is not valid and does not have this effect that he described unless it is connected to the oath, which is the point of agreement with al-Tabari's interpretation. This is the view of Ibrahim, Ata and al-Sha'bi, "because the exception is in the position of a condition. It is not suitable, and its ruling is not established, except when it is joined to the speech without a pause, like saying: 'You are divorced if you enter the house.' If he said: 'You are divorced,' then said, 'If you enter the house,' after remaining silent, that would not make the divorce depend on entering. His saying, may He be exalted and glorified, ﴿And they remained in their cave﴾, means: the People of the Cave. Some said: this is a report about the People of the Book, that they said that. Had it been a report from Allah, exalted and glorified, about the amount of their stay, His saying "Say: Allah knows best how long they remained" would have had no purpose. This is the view of Qatadah. What supports it is the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "And they said, they remained in their cave." Then Allah, exalted, replied to them, saying: "Say: Allah knows best how long they remained." [[There is room for scrutiny in what Qatadah said. What is in the hands of the People of the Book is that they remained three hundred years without nine, by which they mean solar years. Had Allah, exalted, been relating their statement, He would not have said "and they added nine." The apparent meaning of the verse is only an informing from Allah, not a relating of their words, as in the following view which the author (al-Baghawi) preferred, and it is the choice of al-Tabari, may Allah have mercy on him. Others said: this is an informing from Allah, exalted, about the length of their stay in the cave, and this is the more correct view.

As for His saying: "Say: Allah knows best how long they remained," its meaning is that the matter of the length of their stay is as we have mentioned. If they dispute with you about it, then answer them and say: "Allah knows best how long they remained," meaning: He knows better than you, and He has informed us of the length of their stay.

It was also said: the People of the Book said that this period, from the time they entered the cave until today, is three hundred and nine years. So Allah replied to them and said: "Say: Allah knows best how long they remained," meaning: after the taking of their souls until this day, none knows it but Allah. 218/a

His saying, exalted be He: ﴿three hundred years﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "thalathamia" without tanwin, and the others read it with tanwin.

If it is asked: why did He say "three hundred years" and not "a year"?

It is said: when His saying "And they remained in their cave three hundred" was revealed, they asked: days, months, or years? Then "years" was revealed.

Al-Farra' said: among the Arabs there are those who place "sinin" (years) in the position of "sanah" (year).

It was also said: its meaning is "And they remained in their cave, years, three hundred."

﴿And they added nine﴾. Al-Kalbi [[al-Kalbi is Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib, weak. See also: Zad al-Masir: 5/131.]] said: the Christians of Najran said: as for the three hundred, we know it, but as for the nine, we have no knowledge of it, so it was revealed.

Qur'anic quotations, names of persons, and technical terms are rendered as the system instructions require. Here is the translation:

﴿Say: "Allah knows best how long they stayed."﴾ It is narrated from Ali that he said: "According to the People of the Book, they stayed three hundred solar years, while Allah, the Exalted, mentioned three hundred lunar years. The difference between the solar and lunar years is three years in every hundred years, so in three hundred years there is a difference of nine years. For this reason He said: ﴿and they added nine [years]﴾."

﴿To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth.﴾ The "unseen" (ghayb) is that which is hidden from perception, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, nothing is hidden from His perception.

﴿How clearly He sees, and how clearly He hears!﴾ That is: how perfectly Allah sees every existing thing, and how perfectly He hears everything that is heard. That is, nothing is hidden from His hearing and His sight.

﴿They have no one besides Him﴾, that is, the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth have no one besides Allah ﴿as a protector﴾, a helper. ﴿And He does not make anyone a partner in His judgment.﴾ Ibn 'Amir and Ya'qub read "وَلَا تُشْرِكْ" with a ta' (second person, prohibition), while the others read it with a ya' (third person), meaning: Allah does not make anyone a partner in His judgment. It was also said that "al-hukm" (judgment) here means knowledge of the unseen, that is, He does not make anyone a partner in His knowledge of the unseen.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Recite﴾, and read, O Muhammad, ﴿what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord﴾, meaning the Qur'an, and follow what is in it. ﴿None can alter His words﴾. Al-Kalbi said: none can change the Qur'an. It was also said: none can change what He has threatened with His words for the people of disobedience.

﴿And you will not find﴾, you, ﴿besides Him﴾, if you do not follow the Qur'an, ﴿any refuge (multaḥad)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: a shelter (ḥirz). Al-Hasan said: an entrance. Mujahid said: a place of refuge. It was said: a means of deviation. It was said: a place of escape. Its root is from inclination (al-mayl).

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And keep yourself patient﴾ (the verse). It was revealed concerning 'Uyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari, who came to the Prophet ﷺ before he had embraced Islam, while with him was a group of the poor, among them Salman. He was wearing a woolen cloak, in which he was sweating, and in his hand was a palm-leaf fiber that he was splitting and then weaving. 'Uyayna said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Does the smell of these people not bother you? We are the chiefs and nobles of Mudar. If we embrace Islam, the people will embrace Islam with us, and nothing prevents us from following you except these people. So push them away from you until we follow you, or make for us a gathering and for them a gathering." So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And keep yourself patient﴾ [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/380–382; al-Tabari: 15/234–236; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, pp. 344–345; Zad al-Masir: 5/132.]], that is: restrain yourself, O Muhammad, ﴿with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening﴾, the two ends of the day, ﴿seeking His Face﴾, that is: seeking Allah, not seeking any worldly gain.

Qatadah said: it was revealed concerning the People of the Suffah (Ahl al-Suffah), who were seven hundred poor men in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They did not return to trade, nor to crops, nor to livestock. They would pray one prayer and wait for another. When this verse was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ said: "Praise be to Allah who has placed among my community those with whom I was commanded to keep myself patient" [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/380; Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 345; Ibn Kathir: 3/82.]].

﴿And do not let your eyes pass beyond them﴾, that is: do not turn away from them, nor go beyond them, to others, ﴿desiring the adornment of the worldly life﴾, that is: seeking the company of the wealthy and nobles, and the companionship of the people of this world.

﴿And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance﴾, that is: whose heart We have made neglectful of Our remembrance, meaning 'Uyayna ibn Hisn. It was also said: Umayya ibn Khalaf. ﴿And who follows his desire﴾, that is: his aim in pursuing desires. ﴿And whose affair has been [ufuran]﴾. Qatadah and Mujahid said: lost. It was said: its meaning is that he wasted his affair and neglected his days. It was said: regret. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: extravagance. Al-Farra' said: abandoned. It was said: false. It was said: opposing the truth. Al-Akhfash said: exceeding the limit. ﴿And say: The truth is from your Lord﴾ meaning: what has been mentioned of faith and the Qur'an. Its meaning: Say, O Muhammad, to these people whose hearts We have made heedless of Our remembrance: O people, [the truth has come to you from your Lord] [[In "B": The truth is from your Lord.]] and with Him is success and failure, and in His hand is guidance and misguidance; none of that is up to me.

﴿So whoever wills, let him believe; and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾ This is in the manner of a threat and warning, like His saying: "Do what you will" [Fussilat: 40] [[Said by al-Zajjaj. See: Zad al-Masir: 5/134; Ibn Kathir: 3/82.]].

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tawba informed us: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith informed us: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kisa'i informed us: Abdullah ibn Mahmud informed us: Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khallal informed us: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, from Rishdin ibn Sa'd, related to us: Amr ibn al-Harith related to me, from Darraj ibn Abi al-Samh, from Abu al-Haytham ibn Abdullah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "The enclosure of the Fire is four walls, the thickness of each wall is like a journey of forty years." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the chapters on the description of Hell, chapter on what has come regarding the description of the drink of the people of the Fire: 7/306, and he said: "This is a hadith we only know from the narration of Rishdin, and there is criticism of Rishdin ibn Sa'd." It was also narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 3/29, al-Hakim: 4/601, al-Tabari: 15/239, and the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 15/245. Ibn Abbas said: it is a wall of fire.

al-Kalbi said: it is a neck that comes out of the Fire and encircles the disbelievers like an enclosure.

Ibn Abbas said: it is thick water like the sediment of oil.

Mujahid said: it is pus and blood.
