The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 18, verses 30–32:

God Most High says: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—indeed, We do not allow to be lost the reward of one who does good work.﴾ If it is asked: where is the response (jawab, the main clause that completes the conditional sentence) to His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾?

It is said: its response is His saying: ﴿those—for them are gardens of perpetual residence, beneath which rivers flow﴾. As for His saying: ﴿indeed, We do not allow to be lost﴾, it is a parenthetical statement (kalam mu'taridh, an interjected clause) [[Zad al-Masir: 5/137.]].

It is also said: there is an omitted element (idmar, an implied ellipsis) in it, its meaning being: "Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—then indeed We do not allow their reward to be lost, but We recompense them." Then He mentioned the recompense, saying: [[Zad al-Masir: 5/137.]]

﴿Those—for them are gardens of 'Adn﴾, that is, a place of abiding. It is said: "'Adana fulan bil-makan" when someone settles in a place. They are called 'Adn because the believers remain in them forever. ﴿Beneath them rivers flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: each one of them will be adorned with three bracelets: one of gold, one of silver, and one of pearls and rubies. ﴿And they will wear green garments of fine silk﴾, which is what is thin of brocade (dibaj), ﴿and brocade﴾, which is what is thick of it. The meaning of thickness in the garments of Paradise is its firmness. On the authority of Abu 'Imran al-Jawni, who said: sundus is brocade woven with gold. ﴿Reclining therein﴾, in the Gardens, ﴿upon couches﴾, which are thrones (surur) within canopies (hijal), singular ara'ika. ﴿How excellent the reward!﴾, that is, how excellent the recompense. ﴿And how good a resting place﴾, the Gardens, ﴿a place of repose (murtafaq)﴾, that is, a sitting place and an abode.

﴿And present to them the parable of two men﴾, the verse. It is said: it was revealed concerning two brothers from the people of Makkah from the Banu Makhzum, one of whom was a believer, namely Abu Salamah 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Asad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 6/124.]], [and he was the husband of Umm Salamah before the Prophet ﷺ, and the other was a disbeliever, namely al-Aswad ibn 'Abd al-Asad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth] [[What is between the brackets is omitted from "B".]].

It is also said: this is a parable for 'Uyaynah ibn Hisn and his companions with Salman and his companions. He likened them to two men from the Children of Israel, two brothers, one of whom was a believer, named Yahudha according to the statement of Ibn 'Abbas. Muqatil said: Yamlikha. The other was a disbeliever, named Qutrus. Wahb said: Qitfir. These are the two whom God Most High described in Surat al-Saffat. Their story, as 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak related from Ma'mar from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, was: there were two partners who had eight thousand dinars. It is also said: they were two brothers who inherited eight thousand dinars from their father, and they divided it. One of them purposely bought land for a thousand dinars, and his companion said: "O God, so-and-so has bought land for a thousand dinars, so I buy from You land in Paradise for a thousand dinars," and he gave a thousand dinars in charity. Then his companion built a house for a thousand dinars, and the other said: "O God, so-and-so has built a house for a thousand dinars, so I buy from You a house in Paradise for a thousand dinars," and he gave that in charity. Then his companion married a woman and spent a thousand dinars on her, and this believer said: "O God, I propose to You a woman from the women of Paradise for a thousand dinars," and he gave a thousand dinars in charity. Then his companion bought servants and goods for a thousand dinars, and this one said: "O God, I buy from You goods and servants in Paradise for a thousand dinars," and he gave a thousand dinars in charity. Then a severe need befell him, and he said: "If only I went to my companion, perhaps he would bestow some kindness upon me." He sat on his path until he passed by him with his retinue. He got up toward him, and the other looked at him and recognized him, and said: "So-and-so?" He said: "Yes." He said: "What is your condition?" He said: "A need has befallen me after you, so I came to you that you might grant me some good." He said: "What has become of your wealth, when we divided one wealth and you took half of it?" So he related to him his story. He said: "And are you really among those who believe in this?! Go away, I will not give you anything," and he drove him off. Then it was decreed for both of them that they died, and there was revealed concerning them: "Then some of them will approach others, questioning one another. A speaker among them will say: Indeed, I had a companion" (al-Saffat 50–51) [[Ma bayna al-qawsayn saqit min "A".]].

It was also related that when he came to him, he took him by the hand and began to walk around with him, showing him the wealth of his own self, and so it was revealed concerning the two of them [[See: Zad al-Masir: 5/138–139; al-Bahr al-Muhit: 6/124; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/399–400. The story is from the narration of al-Kalbi, who is weak.]].

The hifaf (surrounding border) is the side, its plural being ahiffah. It is said: "hafffa bihi al-qawm," meaning: the people went around its sides. ﴿And We placed between them cultivated land﴾, that is, We placed the palm trees around the grapevines and the crops in the midst of the grapevines.

It is also said: "between them" means between the two gardens, cultivated land, meaning: there was no barren place between the two gardens.

**Al-Baghawi's Commentary (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 18, verses 33–36:**

﴿Each of the two gardens brought forth its produce﴾, i.e., each of the two gardens gave its fruit in full, ﴿and did not fall short therein in anything﴾, i.e., did not diminish any of it. ﴿And We caused a river to gush forth through their midst﴾: the common reading is with the shadda (tashdid) on the jim, while Ya'qub read it with the jim lightened (takhfif). It means: We split the ground and brought forth a river through the middle of the two of them.

﴿And he had fruit﴾, i.e., the owner of the garden had fruit. ʿĀṣim, Abu Ja'far and Ya'qub read ﴿thamar﴾ with a fatha on the tha' and the mim, and likewise "bi-thamarihi". Abu 'Amr read it with a damma on the tha' and the mim sukun. The others read both with a damma.

Whoever reads it with a fatha, it is the plural of thamara (a single fruit), which is what a tree produces of edible fruits.

Whoever reads it with a damma, it is abundant productive wealth of every kind, the plural of thimar. Mujahid said: gold and silver. It was also said: all kinds of fruits.

Al-Azhari said: "thamara" is pluralized as "thamar," and "thamar" is pluralized as "thimar," then "thimar" is pluralized as "thumur" [[See: Lisan al-Arab: 4/107, entry "th-m-r".]].

﴿He said﴾, i.e., the owner of the garden, ﴿to his companion﴾, the believer, ﴿while he was conversing with him﴾, addressing him and replying to him: ﴿I am greater than you in wealth and mightier in numbers (nafar)﴾, i.e., in kinsfolk and clan. Qatadah said: servants and attendants. Muqatil said: children, and its corroboration is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If you see me as less than you in wealth and children﴾ [al-Kahf: 39].

﴿And he entered his garden﴾, i.e., the disbeliever took his brother, the Muslim, by the hand, walking him around in it and showing him its fruits, ﴿while he was wronging himself﴾ by his disbelief. ﴿He said: I do not think that this will ever perish﴾, i.e., be destroyed, ﴿ever﴾. The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: its beauty pleased him and its splendor deceived him, so he imagined that it would never perish, and he denied the Resurrection. So he said: ﴿Nor do I think the Hour will be established﴾, i.e., coming to pass. ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than it as a destination﴾. The people of the Hijaz and Syria read it this way in the dual, meaning "than the two gardens," and likewise it is written so in their codices; the others read ﴿minha﴾, i.e., than the garden he entered, ﴿as a destination﴾, i.e., a place of return.

If it is asked: how did he say, "And if I am returned to my Lord," when he denied the Resurrection?

It is said: its meaning is, "And if I am returned to my Lord, as you claim, He will give me there something better than it, for He did not give me this garden in this world except that He would give me something better than it in the Hereafter."

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verses 37–40:**

﴿His companion said to him﴾, the Muslim, ﴿while he was disputing with him: "Do you disbelieve in He who created you from dust"﴾, meaning, He created your origin from dust, ﴿then﴾ He created you ﴿from a drop [of semen], then fashioned you into a man﴾, meaning: He made you complete, a human being, sound, male.

﴿But as for me, He is Allah, my Lord﴾. Ibn 'Amir and Ya'qub recited "lakinna" with an alif in连接 speech (wasl, connected reading), while the rest read it without an alif. They all agreed on keeping the alif in pause (waqf, stopping at the end of a word). Its original form is "lakinna ana," so the hamza was dropped to lighten the word because it was used so frequently, and then one of the two nuns was assimilated into the other (idgham). Al-Kisa'i said: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in it, and its meaning is: "lakinna Allahu huwa rabbi." ﴿And I do not associate anyone with my Lord﴾.

﴿Why, when you entered your garden, did you not say: "Whatever Allah wills [will happen]"﴾, meaning: why did you not say, when you entered your garden, "Whatever Allah wills"? It is said: "Whatever Allah wills" means: the matter is what Allah wills. It is also said that its response is implied, meaning: whatever Allah wills, occurs. His words ﴿There is no power except with Allah﴾ mean: I have no power to preserve my wealth or to ward off anything from it, except [by the permission of Allah] [[In "B": "with Allah."]].

It is narrated from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, that whenever he saw something from his wealth that pleased him, or entered one of his orchards, he would say: "Whatever Allah wills; there is no power except with Allah." [[Reported by Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in "Shu'ab al-Iman." See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/391.]]

Then he said: ﴿If you see me as less than you in wealth and children﴾. The word "ana" [I] is a separator pronoun ('imad, a pronoun that separates a subject from its predicate), and for this reason "aqall" is in the accusative. Its meaning: if you see me as less than you in wealth and children, then you have become arrogant and exalted yourself over me.

﴿Perhaps my Lord﴾, meaning: so perhaps my Lord ﴿will give me﴾, meaning, will bestow on me in the Hereafter, ﴿something better than your garden, and will send upon it﴾, meaning: upon your garden, ﴿a calamity﴾ (husban). Qatadah said: a punishment. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: fire. Al-Qutabi said: projectiles (marami) ﴿from the sky﴾. It is like a thunderbolt or something that destroys it. Its singular is "husbanah."

﴿So that it becomes bare ground, slippery﴾, meaning: a barren, smooth land with no vegetation in it. It is also said: feet slip on it. Mujahid said: a vast heap of sand.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 41–44:

﴿Or its water should become sunken﴾, meaning: sunk into the earth, cut off, gone away, so that hands cannot reach it nor buckets. ﴿And his fruits were encompassed [by ruin]﴾, meaning: the punishment encompassed the fruits of his garden. That is, he is not able to help himself. It was also said: he is not able to restore what had gone from him.

﴿There, guardianship belongs to God, the True﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "al-wilayah" with a kasra on the waw, meaning sovereignty. The others read it with a kasra as an adjective of God, as in His saying: ﴿Then they are returned to God, their true Master﴾ [al-An'am: 62].

﴿He is best in reward﴾, meaning: the best recompense for the people of His obedience, even if another were to reward. ﴿And best in outcome﴾, meaning: the outcome of obeying Him is better than the outcome of obeying others, so He is better in giving reward. "Uqban" (outcome): obedience is its meaning. Hamzah and 'Asim read "uqban" with a sukun on the qaf, and the others read it with a damma.

That is because God, exalted is He, sent a fire upon it, and it destroyed it, and its water sank. ﴿So he began﴾, its owner, the disbeliever, ﴿turning over his palms﴾, meaning: he clapped one hand against the other and turned his palms over, back and front, in regret and distress ﴿over what he had spent on it, while it lay in ruins upon its trellises﴾, meaning: fallen down upon its roofs. ﴿And he said: "Would that I had not associated anyone with my Lord."﴾ God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And he had no group to help him against God﴾, meaning: a company ﴿who would support him other than God﴾, meaning: who would protect him from the punishment of God. ﴿And he was not one who could defend himself﴾, meaning: unable to resist and avenge himself. That is, he is not able to help himself. It was also said: he is not able to restore what had gone from him.

﴿There, guardianship belongs to God, the True﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "al-wilayah" with a kasra on the waw, meaning sovereignty. The others read it with a fatha on the waw, from "al-muwalah" (loyalty) and "al-nasr" (support), as in God's saying: ﴿God is the Ally of those who believe﴾ [al-Baqarah: 257]. Al-Qutaybi said: he means that they will turn to Him on that day and disown what they used to worship.

It was also said: with the fatha, it means lordship (al-rububiyyah), and with the kasra, it means rule (al-imarah).

﴿Al-haqq﴾ with a raised qaf (al-haqqu): Abu 'Amr and al-Kisa'i, as an adjective of "al-wilayah." Confirming this is the reading of Ubayy: ﴿There, guardianship is for God, the Truth﴾. The others read it with a kasra as an adjective of God, as in His saying: ﴿Then they are returned to God, their true Master﴾ [al-An'am: 62].

﴿He is best in reward﴾, meaning: the best recompense for the people of His obedience, even if another were to reward. ﴿And best in outcome﴾, meaning: the outcome of obeying Him is better than the outcome of obeying others, so He is better in giving reward. "Uqban" (outcome): obedience is its meaning. Hamzah and 'Asim read "uqban" with a sukun on the qaf, and the others read it with a damma.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verses 45–46:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And present to them the parable of the life of this world: it is like water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, and then it becomes dry stubble which the winds scatter.﴾ O Muhammad, that is, to your people. ﴿Like water which We send down from the sky﴾ means the rain. ﴿The vegetation of the earth mingles with it﴾: every kind of color and flower emerges from it. ﴿Then it becomes﴾ soon after ﴿dry stubble﴾, meaning dried up. Ibn Abbas said, and al-Dahhak said: broken into pieces. Al-Hashim (dry stubble) is that which has dried out and crumbled from the plants, so it becomes dry stubble. ﴿Which the winds scatter﴾: Ibn Abbas said, the winds stir it up [[In "B": "tudiruhu" (turns it around).]]. Abu Ubayda said: they disperse it. Al-Qutaybi said: they blow it away. ﴿And Allah is ever Able over all things﴾: Capable.

﴿Wealth and children﴾, by which Utbah and his wealthy companions boast, ﴿are the adornment of the life of this world﴾; they are not part of the provision for the Hereafter.

Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Wealth and children are the tilth of this world, and righteous deeds are the tilth of the Hereafter, and Allah may combine them for some peoples.

﴿And the enduring good deeds﴾: they differed concerning them. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah and Mujahid said: they are the saying "Subhan Allah (Glory be to Allah), al-hamdu lillah (praise be to Allah), la ilaha illa Allah (there is no god but Allah), and Allahu akbar (Allah is greatest)." It has been related to us that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The best speech is four words: Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, and Allahu akbar" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in suspended form in al-Ayman wal-Nudhur: 11/566; it was linked by al-Nasa'i through the route of Dirar ibn Murrah from Abu Salih from Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayrah, raised to the Prophet, with the same wording. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Samurah ibn Jundub: 3/1675 with the wording "beloved" (ahabb) instead of "best" (afdal). Ibn Hibban narrated it through this route with the wording "best." The hadith of Abu Hurayrah has other routes, narrated by al-Nasa'i and authenticated by Ibn Hibban. See Fath al-Bari: 11/567.]].

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hanafi informed us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us: Abu Ja'far Abdullah ibn Isma'il al-Hashimi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Attaridi informed us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "To say Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, and Allahu akbar is dearer to me than everything upon which the sun rises" [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Dhikr wal-Du'a wal-Tawbah, chapter on the virtue of tahlil, tasbih and supplication, no. (2695): 4/2072. The author also in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/60.]].

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us: Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar informed us: Humayd ibn Zanjuwayh informed us: Uthman narrated to us, from Abu Salih: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us: Darraj narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "Increase in the enduring good deeds." It was said: "And what are they, O Messenger of Allah?" [He said: "The religion (al-milla)." It was said: "And what is it, O Messenger of Allah?"] [[What is between the brackets is an addition from "B".]] He said: "Takbir, tahlil, tasbih, al-hamdu lillah, and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah al-Aliyy al-Azim (there is no power nor strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Mighty)" [[Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad: 3/75; Ibn Hibban p. (579) from Mawarid al-Zam'an; and al-Hakim: 1/512, who said: "This is the most authentic chain of the Egyptians, though they did not narrate it." Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/87): "Ahmad and Abu Ya'la narrated it... and their chains are good." Al-Mundhiri attributed it in al-Targhib wal-Tarhib (2/431) to Ahmad, Abu Ya'la, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim, and related al-Hakim's authentication of it. The author narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/64-65. It contains Darraj from Abu al-Haytham, and it is weak, but the hadith has corroborating evidence.]].

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Masruq and Ibrahim said: "The enduring good deeds" are the five daily prayers. This is also related from Ibn Abbas [[See al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/399; Zad al-Masir: 5/149.]].

And there is another narration from him: that they are the righteous deeds [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/399.]], and this is the saying of Qatadah.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Better in the sight of your Lord for reward﴾, that is, for recompense, ﴿and better for hope﴾, that is, what a person hopes for.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And present to them the parable of the life of this world: it is like water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, and then it becomes dry stubble which the winds scatter.﴾ O Muhammad, that is, to your people. ﴿Like water which We send down from the sky﴾ means the rain. ﴿The vegetation of the earth mingles with it﴾: every kind of color and flower emerges from it. ﴿Then it becomes﴾ soon after ﴿dry stubble﴾, meaning dried up. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 47:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿And the Day We set the mountains in motion﴾. Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and Ibn 'Amir read "tusayyaru" (are set in motion) with a ta' and a fathah on the ya', so that ﴿the mountains﴾ is in the nominative (raf'). Its evidence is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when the mountains are set in motion﴾ [at-Takwir: 3].

The others read it with a nun and a kasrah on the ya', so that "al-jibal" (the mountains) is in the accusative (nasb), and "taysir al-jibal" (moving the mountains) means transporting them from one place to another.

﴿And you will see the earth laid bare﴾, meaning: apparent, with no tree, no mountain and no vegetation upon it, as He said: "And He will leave it a level plain, in which you will see no crookedness or elevation" [Ta-Ha: 107].

'Ata' said: it is the emergence of what is within it of the dead and others, so you will see the inside of the earth become apparent.

﴿And We will gather them﴾ all together to the place of standing and reckoning, ﴿and We will not leave out from them﴾, meaning: We will not leave behind from them, ﴿anyone﴾.

[[Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 48:]]

﴿And they will be presented before your Lord in rows﴾. That is, row after row, company after company, not that they will be one single row. It is also said: standing. Then it will be said to them, meaning the disbelievers: ﴿You have certainly come to Us as We created you the first time﴾, meaning alive. It is also said: alone, as is mentioned in Surat al-An'am [[See the commentary on verse (94) of Surat al-An'am: 3 / 169.]]. It is also said: ghurlan (uncircumcised, the Arabic word غُرْلًا).

﴿Rather, you claimed that We would never appoint for you an appointed time﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection. This is said to those who deny the resurrection.

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, who was told by Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi, who was told by Muhammad ibn Yusuf, who was told by Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who was told by Mu'alla ibn Asad, who was told by Wahb, from Ibn Tawus, from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "People will be gathered on three paths: those who are eager and those who are fearful; two on one camel, three on one camel, four on one camel, ten on one camel; and the Fire will gather the rest of them. It will rest when they rest, it will spend the night with them where they spend the night, it will be with them in the morning where they are in the morning, and it will be with them in the evening where they are in the evening." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Riqaq, chapter on the Gathering (al-Hashr): 11 / 377, and Muslim in al-Jannah wa Sifat Na'imiha wa Ahliha, no. (2861): 4 / 2195, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15 / 124-125.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, who was told by Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi, who was told by Muhammad ibn Yusuf, who was told by Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who was told by Muhammad ibn Kathir, who was told by Sufyan ibn al-Mughira ibn al-Nu'man, who was told by Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed you will be gathered barefoot, naked and uncircumcised (ghurlan)." Then he recited: "As We began the first creation, We will repeat it; a promise upon Us. Indeed, We will be doing it." [al-Anbiya': 104] "And the first to be clothed on the Day of Resurrection will be Ibrahim. Some men from my companions will be taken to the left side, and I will say: 'My companions, my companions!' It will be said: 'Indeed, they have not ceased to turn back on their heels since you parted from them.' So I will say what the righteous servant said: 'And I was a witness over them while I was among them' up to his saying: 'the Mighty, the Wise.'" [al-Ma'idah: 117-118] [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Anbiya', chapter on the saying of Allah, "And Allah took Ibrahim as a friend": 6 / 386, and Muslim in al-Jannah wa Sifat Na'imiha wa Ahliha, chapter on the annihilation of this world and the explanation of the Day of Gathering, no. (2680): 4 / 2194-2195, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15 / 123.]]

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi [informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Sarakhsi informed us] [[Dropped from manuscript "a".]] informed us, Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mughallis in Baghdad informed us, who was told by Harun ibn Ishaq al-Hamadhani, who was told by Abu Khalid al-Ahmar, from Hatim ibn Abi Saghir, from Ibn Abi Mulayka, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aisha, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how will people be gathered on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "Naked and barefoot." She said: I said: "And the women?" He said: "And the women." She said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, we will be ashamed!" He said: "O Aisha, the matter is too grave for that; it will preoccupy them so that none of them looks at another." [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Jannah wa Sifat Na'imiha wa Ahliha, chapter on the annihilation of this world and the explanation of the Gathering, no. (2859): 15 / 124.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 49:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the Book will be placed﴾, meaning: the books of the deeds of the servants [[In "B": their deeds.]] will be placed in the hands of people, in their right hands and their left hands. It was also said: its meaning is that it will be placed before Allah, exalted is He. ﴿So you will see the criminals fearful﴾, afraid ﴿of what is in it﴾ of the evil deeds, ﴿and they will say﴾ when they see them: ﴿O woe to us!﴾, O our destruction. "Al-wayl" and "al-waylah" mean destruction, and whoever falls into destruction calls out "woe." The meaning of the call (nida') is to alert the listeners. ﴿What is this Book that leaves neither a small thing nor a great thing﴾ of our sins [unrecorded]. Ibn 'Abbas said: "The small thing (saghirah)" is the smile, and "the great thing (kabirah)" is the loud laughter. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The small thing" is the lamam (minor lapses), the touching and the kiss, and "the great thing" is fornication.

﴿Except that it has enumerated it﴾, counted it [[Omitted in "B".]]. Al-Suddi said: it wrote it down and recorded it. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: it preserved it.

Al-Imam Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us, saying: Abu al-'Abbas 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Harun al-Tay sifuni informed us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Turabi informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Bastam informed us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Yasar al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn 'Udayy al-Misri narrated to us, saying: Abu Damrah Anas ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, who said: "I do not know it except from Sahl ibn Sa'd," who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of belittled sins, for the likeness of belittled sins is the likeness of a people who camped in the bottom of a valley; one came with a stick and another came with a stick, until they baked their bread. Indeed, belittled sins are destructive ones [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 5/331, and its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih. Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Thalathah by two routes, and the narrators of one of them are the narrators of the Sahih except 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Abd al-Hakam, who is trustworthy. See: Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/190. The author also cited it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/399.]]."

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will find what they did present﴾, written down and recorded in their book. ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾, meaning: the reward of no one who has done good will be diminished.

Al-Dahhak said: He does not hold anyone accountable for a crime he did not commit.

'Abd Allah ibn Qays said: "People will be presented on the Day of Resurrection in three presentations. As for the first two: there will be disputation and excuses. As for the third presentation: then the pages will fly in people's hands, so one takes his book in his right hand and another takes it in his left." Some of them traced it back to Abu Musa [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Zuhd, chapter on what has come concerning the presentation: 7/111, from al-Hasan from Abu Hurayrah, raised to the Prophet. He said: "This hadith is not sound, because al-Hasan did not hear from Abu Hurayrah [so it is disconnected]; and some narrated it from 'Ali ibn 'Ali, who is al-Rifa'i, from al-Hasan from Abu Musa from the Prophet (ﷺ)." Ibn Majah narrated it by this route in al-Zuhd, no. (4277): 2/1430; he said in al-Zawa'id: "Its chain's narrators are trustworthy, except that it is disconnected..." Also Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 4/414. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in "al-Ba'th" with a good chain from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud as a statement of his companion. See: Fath al-Bari: 11/403.]].

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 50:**

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿And [remember] when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam"﴾. He says: Mention, O Muhammad, when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," ﴿so they prostrated, except Iblis. He was of the jinn﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: He was of a group of the angels called the jinn, who were created from the fire of the samum wind.[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 1/502 (Dar al-Maʿarif).]] Al-Hasan said: He was of the jinn and was not of the angels. He is the origin of the jinn, just as Adam is the origin of mankind.[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 1/506. Ibn Kathir said (3/89): "This chain from al-Hasan is sound." Al-Tabari, may Allah have mercy on him, preferred the first opinion, though it seems he preferred the less preferred view, as the author did in 1/82 of this edition. The apparent meaning of the Qur'an is that Iblis was of the jinn and was created from fire. When the word "jinn" is used without qualification, it refers to the known jinn, not to a class of angels called "jinn" created from the fire of the samum. But there is no proof for the soundness of that... Therefore, after Hafiz Ibn Kathir presented the narrations on this, he said (3/90): "Many reports have been transmitted on this from the early generations, referring to the narrations from Ibn ʿAbbas that Iblis was one of the angels created from fire, whose name was al-Jinn. Most of them are from the Isrāʾīliyyāt (narratives of Jewish and Christian origin), which are transmitted so that they may be examined, and Allah knows best the state of many of them. Among them are some whose falsehood can be asserted, because they contradict the truth in our hands. The Qur'an suffices us in place of all other earlier reports, because these are hardly free from alteration, addition and omission. Many things have been fabricated in them, and they have no precise memorizers who can clear them of the distortion of extremists and the forgeries of falsifiers, as this nation has, with its imams, scholars, masters, pious and righteous people, and noble critics, the excellent memorizers who recorded the hadith, verified it, distinguished its sound from its good, its weak, its denounced, its fabricated, its abandoned, and its forged, and who knew the forgers, liars, and unknown transmitters, and the other categories of narrators. All of this is to protect the Prophetic sanctuary and the Muhammadan station, the seal of the messengers and the master of mankind (ﷺ), from being attributed to him with falsehood or from being related from him what is not from him. May Allah be pleased with them and make them content, and make the Gardens of Paradise their abode."]] ﴿So he defied﴾, that is, departed from ﴿the command of his Lord﴾, that is, from obedience to his Lord. ﴿Will you then take him and his descendants as protectors, instead of Me, while they are an enemy to you?﴾ That is, enemies.

Mujalid narrated from al-Shaʿbi, who said: I was sitting one day when a man came and said: "Tell me, does Iblis have a wife?" I said: "I did not witness that wedding." Then I recalled His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Will you then take him and his descendants as protectors, instead of Me?﴾ So I knew that descendants can only come from a wife, and I said: "Yes."

Qatadah said: They reproduce just as the children of Adam reproduce.

It was also said: He inserts his tail into his anus, and he lays an egg, and the egg hatches into a group of devils.

Mujahid said: Among the descendants of Iblis are Laqis and Walhan, who are the companions of purification and prayer; al-Haffaf and Murrah, after whom he is given the kunya (teknonym); Zalanbur, who is the companion of the markets, who adorns vain talk, false oaths, and praise of wares; Thabr, who is the companion of calamities, who adorns the scratching of faces, slapping of cheeks, and tearing of garments; al-Aʿwar, who is the companion of adultery, who blows into the penis of a man and the buttocks of a woman; Mutawwas, who is the companion of false news, who casts it into people's mouths so they find no origin for it; and Dasim, who, when a man enters his house without greeting and without mentioning the name of Allah, blinds him to the goods so that they are not lifted or kept in their place, and when he eats without mentioning the name of Allah, eats with him.[[Narrated from Mujahid by al-Tabari: 15/262. Ibn al-Jawzi and others also mention it: 5/154. There is disagreement about the spelling of some of the names, which we have not indicated since there is no benefit in that. None of these reports has a chain that reaches the infallible one (the Prophet). We are free of them. And Allah knows best.]] Al-Aʿmash said: Sometimes I entered a house without mentioning the name of Allah and without greeting, and I saw a water vessel, so I said, "Remove this," and I argued with them. Then I mentioned the name of Allah and said, "Dasim, Dasim" (meaning he would say to himself that "Dasim" is the one who blinds a person to the goods).[[Al-Tabari: 15/262. That is, he would say to himself that "Dasim" is the one who blinds a person to the goods.]]

It is narrated from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed, there is a devil for wudu' called al-Walhan, so beware of the whisperings of water."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Kitab al-Tahara, chapter on disliking extravagance in water: 1/188-189; Ibn Majah in Kitab al-Tahara, chapter on moderation in wudu': 1/146; Ahmad in al-Musnad: 5/136; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/53. Al-Tirmidhi said in the same place: "The hadith of Ubayy is a gharib hadith, and its chain is not strong. The sound view among the people of hadith is that we know of no one who transmitted it except Kharijah. This hadith has been narrated through other chains from al-Hasan as his own statement. Nothing sound has been transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ) on this subject, and Kharijah is not strong." Al-Dhahabi said in Mizan al-Iʿtidal (1/625): "Kharijah ibn Musʿab: Ahmad rejected him, and Ibn Maʿin said: He is not trustworthy, a liar... He alone transmitted the report, 'Indeed, there is a devil for wudu' called al-Walhan.'"]]

Ismaʿil ibn ʿAbd al-Qahir informed us, who was informed by ʿAbd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad, who was informed by Muhammad ibn ʿIsa al-Juludi, who was informed by Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan, who was informed by Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj, who narrated to us Yahya ibn Khalaf al-Bahili, who was informed by ʿAbd al-Aʿla, from Saʿid al-Jurayri, from Abu al-ʿAla: that ʿUthman ibn Abi al-ʿAs came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the devil has come between me and my prayer and my recitation. He confuses it for me." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "That is a devil called Khinzab. When you sense him, seek refuge in Allah from him, and spit three times to your left." He said: "I did so, and Allah removed him from me."[[Narrated by Muslim in Kitab al-Salam, chapter on seeking refuge from the devil of whispering in prayer, no. (2203): 4/1728-1729.]]

And Ismaʿil ibn ʿAbd al-Qahir informed us, who was informed by ʿAbd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad ibn ʿIsa al-Juludi, who narrated to us Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan, who was informed by Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj, who narrated to us Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn ʿAla, who was informed by Abu Muʿawiya, who narrated to us al-Aʿmash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, may Allah be pleased with them, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Iblis places his throne on the water, then he sends out his detachments. The closest of them to him in rank is the greatest of them in mischief. One of them comes and says, 'I did such and such,' and he says, 'You have done nothing.' Then one of them comes and says, 'I did not leave him until I separated him from his wife,' so he brings him near to himself and says, 'Yes, you are the one.'" Al-Aʿmash said: "I think he said: 'So he embraces him.'"[[Narrated by Muslim in Kitab Sifat al-Munafiqin wa Ahkamihim, chapter on the incitement of Satan and his sending out of detachments, no. (2813): 4/2167. The author also narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/410.]]

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Wretched is the exchange for the wrongdoers.﴾ Qatadah said: How wretched is what they substituted: the obedience of Iblis and his descendants in place of worshipping their Lord.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 51:

﴿مَا أَشْهَدْتُهُمْ﴾ "I did not make them witness" – means: I did not bring them to be present. Abu Ja'far read "مَا أَشْهَدْنَاهُمْ" (mā ashhadnāhum) with a nūn and an alif, in the plural of majesty (ʿalā al-taʿẓīm), meaning: "We did not bring them to be present," referring to Iblis and his offspring. It is also said: the disbelievers. al-Kalbi said: it refers to the angels. ﴿خَلْقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَلَا خَلْقَ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ "the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves." He says: I did not make them witness the creation, so that I would seek their help in creating them and consult them about it. ﴿وَمَا كُنْتُ مُتَّخِذَ الْمُضِلِّينَ عَضُدًا﴾ "And I would not take those who mislead as helpers." That is: the devils who lead people astray, as ʿaḍud (helpers), meaning: supporters and assistants.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 52–54:

His, the Mighty and Majestic's, saying: ﴿And on the Day He will say﴾. Hamzah read it with the nūn (nā, "We will say"), and the others with the yā' (yā, "He will say"), meaning: Allah will say to them on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Call upon My partners﴾, meaning the idols, ﴿whom you claimed﴾ to be My partners, ﴿so they will call upon them﴾, seeking help from them, ﴿but they will not respond to them﴾, meaning they will not answer them nor help them. ﴿And We will place between them﴾, meaning between the idols and their worshippers. It was also said: between the people of guidance and the people of misguidance. ﴿A barrier (mawbiqan)﴾, a place of destruction; this was said by ʿAṭāʾ and al-Ḍaḥḥāk. Ibn ʿAbbās said: it is a valley in the Fire. Mujāhid said: a valley in Jahannam.

ʿIkrimah said: it is a river in the Fire, flowing with fire, and on its bank are serpents like dark mules.

Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: every barrier between two things is a mawbiq, and its root meaning is destruction; it is said: awbaqahu, meaning he destroyed him.

al-Farrāʾ said: We made their communion in the world a means of their destruction in the Hereafter, and the "bayn" (between) in this view is the communion, like His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Certainly your ties have been severed﴾ (al-Anʿām 6:94), according to the reading of the one who read it in the nominative (rafʿ). [[See these sayings in: Zād al-Masīr: 5/158–159.]]

﴿And the criminals will see the Fire﴾, meaning the polytheists, ﴿and they will be certain﴾ (fa-ẓannū, here meaning they were certain) ﴿that they are going to fall into it﴾, entering it and falling into it, ﴿and they will find no escape from it﴾, no way of turning away, because it will encompass them from every side.

His, the Mighty and Majestic's, saying: ﴿And We have certainly diversified﴾, meaning made clear, ﴿in this Qur'an for the people every kind of example﴾, that they may remember and take admonition. ﴿And man has been, most of all things, contentious﴾, meaning given to dispute in falsehood.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: it refers to al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith and his disputing about the Qur'an.

al-Kalbī said: it refers to Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumaḥī. [[Zād al-Masīr: 5/159.]]

It was also said: the meaning of the verse is the disbelievers, because of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve dispute with falsehood﴾ (al-Kahf 18:56).

It was also said: it is general in meaning, and this is the most sound view.

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Aḥmad al-Malīḥī, who said: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Nuʿaymī informed us, who said: Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf informed us, who said: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl informed us, who said: Abū al-Yamān informed us, who said: Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn informed us, that al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī informed him, that ʿAlī informed him that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) visited him and Fāṭimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), one night, and said: "Will you not pray?" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, our souls are in the hand of Allah; if He wills to raise us, He raises us." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned away when I said that to him and did not answer me. Then I heard him as he was leaving, striking his thigh and saying: ﴿And man has been, most of all things, contentious﴾. [[Narrated by al-Bukhārī in al-Tahajjud, chapter on the Prophet's (ﷺ) urging to pray at night and voluntary prayers without obligation: 3/10.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 55–57:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿And what prevented the people from believing when the guidance came to them﴾. [It refers to] the Qur'an, Islam, and the clarification from Allah, exalted and glorified. It is also said: it refers to the Messenger (ﷺ).

﴿and from asking forgiveness of their Lord, except that there should come upon them the way of the former peoples﴾. That is: Our way of destroying them if they do not believe.

It is also said: [the meaning is] "except that they demand that there come upon them the way of the former peoples, [namely] the direct witnessing of the punishment," as they said: "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment" [al-Anfal: 32].

﴿or that the punishment should come upon them face to face﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: that is, openly, before their eyes. Mujahid said: suddenly. Abu Ja'far and the people of Kufa recited ﴿qubulan﴾ with a damma on the qaf and the ba', as the plural of qabil, meaning: kinds of punishment, one kind after another.

﴿And We do not send the messengers except as bringers of good news and warners. And those who disbelieve dispute with falsehood﴾. Their disputing is their saying: "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?" [al-Isra: 94]. "Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from one of the two cities?" [al-Zukhruf: 31], and what is similar to it. ﴿to refute by it the truth﴾: to nullify by it. The root of "dahd" is slipping; the meaning is that they want to remove by it the truth. ﴿And they took My signs and what they were warned of in mockery﴾: there is an implied element in it, meaning "and what they were warned of by it," which is the Qur'an, [taken] in mockery, that is, as ridicule.

﴿And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the signs of his Lord, then turns away from them﴾: is admonished, ﴿turns away from them﴾: turns his back on them, abandons them, and does not believe in them, ﴿and forgets what his hands have sent forward﴾: that is, the sins he committed before. ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings﴾: wrappings, ﴿lest they understand it﴾: that is, comprehend it; the meaning is so that they do not understand it, ﴿and in their ears is deafness﴾: that is, deafness and heaviness. ﴿And if you call them﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿to guidance﴾: to the religion, ﴿they will never be guided, ever﴾. This is said about peoples whom Allah knew would not believe.

And your Lord is the Forgiving, the Possessor of mercy (﴿ذُو الرَّحْمَةِ﴾, the Possessor of mercy), (*dhu al-ni'mah*), the Possessor of blessing. ﴿If He were to take them to task﴾, that is, punish the disbelievers, ﴿for what they have earned﴾, from sins, ﴿He would have hastened for them the punishment﴾ in this world. ﴿But for them there is an appointed time﴾, meaning the Resurrection and the Reckoning [[In "B": "the resurrection" (al-nushur).]], ﴿they will never find besides Him a refuge﴾, a shelter.

﴿And those cities — We destroyed them when they did wrong﴾, meaning the people of Noah, ʿAd, Thamud, the people of Lot, and others, ﴿and We made for their destruction an appointed time﴾, that is, a fixed term. Abu Bakr recited "li-mahlikihim" with a fatḥah on the *mīm* and the *lām*. Hafs recited it with a fatḥah on the *mīm* and a kasrah on the *lām*, and likewise in Surat al-Naml, "mahlik," meaning "for the time of their destruction" [[Omitted from "B".]]. The others recited it with a ḍammah on the *mīm* and a fatḥah on the *lām*, meaning "for their destruction."

So they took bread and a salted fish, until they reached the rock that is at the junction of the two seas at night. Near it there was a spring called the Water of Life; nothing that this water touches remains without life. When the spirit and coolness of the water reached the fish, it moved in the basket, lived, and entered the sea.

Al-Baghawi's commentary (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 18, verses 61–62:

That is the meaning of His Exalted saying: ﴿When they reached the meeting place of the two seas﴾, that is, Musa and his young companion. ﴿The meeting place between them﴾, that is, between the two bodies of water. ﴿They forgot their fish﴾, that is, they left it behind. The fish was actually with Yusha', and it was he who forgot it. The forgetting is attributed to both of them because they had both taken it as provision for their journey, just as one says: "The people went out to such-and-such a place and carried such-and-such provisions," although only one of them carried it.

﴿So it took its way into the sea, a tunnel﴾, that is, the fish took its path, a passage. [It is narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "The water parted over the path of the fish and became a hole that did not close, and Musa entered the hole following the trace of the fish, and there he found al-Khidr."] [[The words between the brackets are omitted in "B".]] [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur 5/423; Ibn Kathir 3/93.]]

Ibn 'Abbas said: The fish would not touch anything of the sea without that thing drying up, until it became a rock. [[Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3/93.]]

Al-Kalbi said: Yusha' ibn Nun performed ablution from the Spring of Life, and some of that water splashed onto the salted fish in the basket, and it came back to life, then leapt into the water and began to strike with its tail; whatever water its tail struck while it was moving away was dried up.

It has also been related to us that when the two of them reached the rock, they laid their heads down and slept, and the fish stirred, came out, and fell into the sea, and took its way into the sea as a tunnel. Then Allah withheld the flow of the water from the fish, so that it stood over it like an arch. When Musa awoke, his companion forgot to tell him. So they set out until, when it was the next day, [[See: al-Bukhari 8/423.]]

His Exalted saying: ﴿So when they had passed on﴾, that is, passed that place, which is the meeting place of the two seas. ﴿He said﴾, Musa said, ﴿to his young companion: "Bring us our morning meal; indeed we have suffered fatigue from this journey of ours."﴾ That is, our food. Al-ghada' is what is prepared to be eaten in the morning (ghudwah), and al-'ashaa' is what is prepared to be eaten in the evening. ﴿Indeed we have suffered fatigue﴾, that is, exhaustion and hardship. This was because hunger had been placed upon Musa after passing the rock, so that he would remember the fish and return to the place he was seeking.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 18, verses 63–64:**

﴿He said﴾ to him, his young man (fatāhu) and he remembered: ﴿"Do you see? When we took refuge at the rock"﴾. It was a rock located at the appointed place. Ma'qil ibn Ziyad said: "It is the rock that lies beyond the River of Oil (Nahr al-Zayt)." ﴿"Indeed I forgot the fish"﴾, meaning I left it behind and lost it. This was because Yusha', when he saw that from the fish, got up to catch up with Musa and inform him, but he forgot to inform him. So they remained that day until they prayed the noon prayer the next day.

It has been said that there is an ellipsis (idmār) in the verse, its meaning being: "I forgot to mention to you the matter of the fish," then he said:

﴿"And none made me forget it except Satan, that I should mention it"﴾. That is: "And none made me forget to mention to you the matter of the fish except Satan." Hafs recited ﴿أَنْسَانِيهُ﴾ (ansānīhu), and in Surat al-Fath (﴿عَلَيْهُ اللَّهَ﴾) he read it with the ha' pronounced with a dammah (ʿalayhu Allāh).

It has also been said that its meaning is: "He made me forget it so that I would not mention it."

﴿And it took its path into the sea in a marvelous way﴾. It has been said: this is from the words of Yusha', who says: "The fish leapt into the sea and took a passage in it, and I marveled greatly at that."

We have also related in a report: "For the fish there was a tunnel, and for Musa and his young man there was a marvel." [[In the narration of al-Bukhari: "…they found in the sea like an arch, the passage of the fish, so there was a marvel for his young man and a tunnel for the fish." Book of Tafsir, chapter "He said: Do you see when we took refuge at the rock": 8/423.]]

It has also been said: this is from the words of Musa, when Yusha' said to him, "and it took its path into the sea," Musa said to him, "A marvel," as if he were saying: "I am more amazed than a marvel."

Ibn Zayd said: "What is more marvelous than a fish from which people eat openly [[In "B": "dahran" (for ages).]], and then it became alive again after part of it had been eaten?"

﴿He said﴾, Musa: ﴿"That is what we were seeking"﴾, meaning, we were looking for it. ﴿So they went back along their tracks, retracing﴾, meaning they returned, following the trail by which they had come, that is, following it. ﴿And they found a servant from among Our servants﴾. It was said: he was an angel from among the angels. But the correct view, which is reported in the histories and is established from the Prophet (ﷺ), is that he was al-Khidr. [[This was mentioned in the earlier hadiths. See Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Traditions of the Prophets, chapter "Hadith of al-Khidr with Musa (peace be upon him)": 6/431–433. The name is pronounced with a fatha on the kha' and a kasra on the dad, and it is permissible to make the dad sakin with the kha' kasra or fatha.]] His name is Balya ibn Malkan. [[See: al-Ma'arif of Ibn Qutaybah, p. 42; Tahdhib al-Asma' wa'l-Lughat of al-Nawawi: 1/176; Fath al-Bari: 6/433.]] It was said: he was from the lineage of the Children of Israel. It was also said: he was one of the sons of the kings who renounced the world. "Al-Khidr" is a title for him, and he was named so because of what follows:

We were informed by Abu 'Ali Hassan ibn Sa'id al-Mani'i, who was informed by Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammash al-Ziyadi, who was informed by Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan, who related to us Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami, who related to us 'Abd al-Razzaq, who was informed by Ma'mar, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: Abu Hurayra related to us, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He was only named Khidr because he sat upon a white pelt (farwa bayḍā'), and it suddenly shook beneath him and became green (khadra')." [[Related by al-Bukhari in the chapter on the Traditions of the Prophets, "Hadith of al-Khidr with Musa": 6/433.]]

Mujahid said: "He was named Khidr because whenever he prayed, what was around him turned green."

We have also related that Musa saw al-Khidr covered with a garment, so he greeted him. Al-Khidr said: "And how is peace in your land?" He said: "I am Musa. I have come to you so that you may teach me of what you have been taught, of right guidance." [[The transmission of this report and the one that follows has been mentioned previously.]]

In another narration, he met him covered with a garment, lying on his back, with part of the garment under his head and part under his feet. In another narration, he met him while he was praying. It is also reported that he met him on a green carpet (ṭunfusa khaḍrā') on the surface of the sea. This is the reason for the words of the Exalted: ...

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 65:

﴿So they found a servant from among Our servants, whom We had given mercy from Us﴾, meaning a blessing, ﴿and taught him knowledge from Our presence﴾, meaning: the knowledge of the inner reality (ʿilm al-bāṭin), by inspiration (ilhām). Al-Khiḍr was not a prophet according to most of the people of knowledge.[[There is disagreement among the scholars concerning al-Khiḍr: whether he is a prophet or not, and whether he remains alive until now and until the Day of Resurrection. Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ inclined to his continued life. They mentioned stories and reports about him from the salaf and others, and some hadiths mention him, meaning that he is alive, but none of that is authentic, and the most famous of them is the hadith of condolence (ḥadīth al-taʿziyah), whose chain is weak. Others among the muḥaddithūn held the opposite view, and [argued] that it has not been reported that he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), nor attended his presence, nor fought alongside him. Had he been alive, he would have been among the followers and companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), because he, peace be upon him, was sent to all of the two weighty groups (al-thaqalayn): the jinn and humankind. He (ﷺ) said: "If Musa and ʿIsa were alive, they would have had no choice but to follow me." He also informed, shortly before his death, that no one who is upon the face of the earth would remain after a hundred years from that night, not one eye that blinks, and other evidences. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verses 66–71:

﴿Musa said to him, "May I follow you so that you may teach me some of what you have been taught, as guidance?"﴾ He means: I came to you so that I may follow you and accompany you. ﴿As guidance﴾: Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub read "rashadan" with a fatha on the ra' and the shin. The others read it with a damma on the ra' and a sukun on the shin, meaning "correctness" (sawaban). It was also said: knowledge by which you guide me.

In some reports, when Musa said this, al-Khidr said to him: "The Torah is enough knowledge for you, and the Children of Israel are enough of a burden." Musa said to him: "Indeed, Allah has commanded me to do this." Then ﴿he said: "Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me."﴾ ﴿He said﴾ to him, al-Khidr: ﴿"Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me."﴾ He only said this because he knew that Musa would see objectionable matters, and it is not permissible for the prophets to remain patient over what is objectionable. Then he explained his excuse for not being patient, saying: ﴿"And how can you be patient about that which you do not comprehend in knowledge?"﴾ That is, knowledge.

﴿Musa said﴾: ﴿"You will find me, if Allah wills, patient"﴾. He made the exception because he was not confident in himself regarding patience. ﴿"And I will not disobey you in any matter."﴾ That is: I will not oppose you in what you command.

﴿He said: "If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything"﴾ — that is, if you accompany me. He did not say "follow me" but left the choice to him, though he imposed a condition on him, saying: ﴿"then do not ask me about anything"﴾. Abu Ja'far, Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read "fala tas'alni" with a fatha on the lam and a shadda on the nun; the others read it with a sukun on the lam and a light nun. ﴿"About anything"﴾ that I do which you find objectionable, and do not object to it, ﴿"until I myself make mention of it to you"﴾, that is, until I begin to mention it to you, and then I will explain its matter to you.

﴿So they set out﴾, walking along the shore seeking a ship to board. They found a ship and boarded it. The people of the ship said: "These are thieves," and they ordered them to disembark. The owner of the ship said: "They are not thieves, but I hope for the faces of the prophets."

We have also related from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "A ship passed by them, and they spoke to them asking to carry them, and they recognized al-Khidr, so they carried them without a fare. When they reached the middle of the sea, al-Khidr took an axe and broke a plank of the ship." [[Previously cited; it is in al-Bukhari, Kitab al-'Ilm: 1/218.]] This is the statement of Allah the Exalted:

﴿Until, when they boarded the ship, he made a hole in it. Musa said to him: "Have you made a hole in it to drown its people?"﴾ Hamza and al-Kisa'i read "liyaghraqa" with a ya' and a fatha, and with a fatha on the ra', and "ahluha" in the nominative, meaning it is intransitive. The others read "latughriqa" with a ta' and a damma, with a kasra on the ra', and "ahlaha" in the accusative, meaning the action is attributed to al-Khidr.

﴿"You have certainly done a terrible thing"﴾ — that is, an objectionable matter. In the speech of the Arabs, "imr" means a calamity, and its origin is: everything that is severe and abundant. It is said: "amira al-qawm" when the people became numerous and their affair became severe.

Al-Qutaybi said: ﴿imran﴾ means: a marvel.

It is related that when al-Khidr made a hole in the ship, water did not enter it. It is also related that when Musa saw this, he took his garment and stuffed the hole with it. It is also related that al-Khidr took a glass bowl and patched the hole of the ship with it.

al-Kalbi said: he was a youth who would commit highway robbery, take goods, and seek refuge with his parents. [[Abu Hayyan said in al-Bahr al-Muhit (1/150): the name of this boy, and the names of his father and mother, have been disputed, and nothing about that has been reported in a hadith.]]

al-Dahhak said: he was a boy who engaged in corruption, and his parents were harmed by him. [[See al-Bahr al-Muhit: 6/150.]]

Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Qahir informed us: 'Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Maslama ibn Mu'attib informed us: Ma'mar ibn Sulayman informed us, from his father, from Ruqayya ibn Mas­qala, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The boy whom al-Khidr killed was sealed as a disbeliever, and had he lived he would have burdened his parents with rebellion and disbelief." [[Related by Muslim in al-Qadar, chapter on the meaning of "Every child is born upon the fitrah," no. (2661): 4/2050.]]

﴿Musa said: "Have you killed a pure soul﴾ Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Abu Ja'far and Abu 'Amr read zakiyatan with an alif (al-zakiyah), while the others read zakiyyatan (zakiyyah). al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' said: the two have the same meaning, like al-qasiyah and al-qasiyyah. Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: al-zakiyah is one who has never sinned at all, and al-zakiyyah is one who sinned and then repented.

﴿without a soul having been killed﴾: that is, he had not killed a soul [for anything] [[Addition from manuscript "b".]] that would make execution obligatory for it.

﴿Indeed you have done a terrible thing (shay'an nukran)﴾: that is, an abhorrent thing. Qatadah said: the nukr is greater than the imr, because it is the very reality of destruction, whereas in the breaking of the ship there was only fear of destruction.

It was also said: the imr is greater, because in it there was the drowning of a great number of people.

Nafi', Ibn 'Amir, Ya'qub and Abu Bakr read here ﴿nukran﴾ [with a sukun], and in Surat al-Talaq with a damma on the kaf; the others read it with a sukun.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 18, verses 75–77:**

﴿He said﴾, meaning al-Khidr: ﴿Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?﴾ It was said that he added "for you" (*laka*) because Moses had broken the covenant twice. In the story, Yusha' (Joshua) used to say to Musa: "O Prophet of Allah, remember the covenant you are under."

﴿He said﴾, Musa: ﴿If I ask you about anything after this﴾, meaning after this time, ﴿then do not keep company with me﴾, meaning part from me. Ya'qub read "fa-la tasbhni" (without the alif), from *suhbah* (companionship).

﴿You have already been given an excuse from my side﴾. Abu Ja'far, Nafi' and Abu Bakr read *min ladunni* with a light nun. The others read it with a doubled nun. Ibn 'Abbas said: that is, "you have been excused regarding what is between me and you."

It was also said: "You warned me that I would not be able to have patience with you." And it was said: "The excuse for my parting from you has become clear to you."

Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Qahir informed us: 'Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn 'Isa informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan told us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj told us: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Qaysi told us: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman told us, from his father, from Ruqayyah, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on us and on Musa." Whenever he mentioned any of the prophets, he began with himself. "Had he been patient, he would have seen the marvels. But he was seized by *dhamamah* [[i.e., shyness and fear of blame and reproach.]] and said: ﴿If I ask you about anything after this, then do not keep company with me; you have been given an excuse from my side﴾. Had he been patient, he would have seen the marvels."[[Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Virtues, chapter on the virtues of al-Khidr, no. (2380/172): 4/185.]]

The words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Then they set out until, when they came to the people of a town﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it means Antioch. Ibn Sirin said: it is al-Ubullah, which is the farthest land from the sky. It was also said: Barqah. And from Abu Hurayrah: a town in al-Andalus. [[The reports differ according to the exegetes' disagreement over which region of the earth the story took place in; Allah knows the reality of this best. See: al-Bahr al-Muhit 6/151; al-Qurtubi 11/24.]] ﴿They asked the people of it for food, but they refused to host them﴾.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Until, when they came to the people of a town that were base, they walked about among the gatherings, and asked its people for food, but they refused to host them." [[A part of the previous hadith.]]

It has also been narrated that they walked around the town asking them for food, but they did not feed them, and they asked for hospitality, but they did not host them.

Qatadah said: the worst of towns is the one that does not host a guest.

It has been narrated from Abu Hurayrah: a woman from the people of Barbar fed them after they had asked the men, who had not fed them. So he (the Prophet) prayed for their women and cursed their men.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿They found in it a wall about to collapse﴾, meaning about to fall. This is a figurative expression of the Arabic language, since a wall has no will; its meaning is that it was close to falling and near collapse, just as the Arabs say: "My house looks onto the house of so-and-so," when it faces it.

﴿So he set it upright﴾, meaning he made it straight. It has been narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Al-Khidr pointed with his hand, and so it was set upright." [[That is: he indicated with his hand and it was set upright. This is an expression of an action by a word, which is common. This is a part of Ubayy's hadith mentioned above in Muslim, and by this this view is preferred over the other views. See: al-Tabari 15/290–291.]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: he wiped the wall with his hand and it became straight. It has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: he demolished it, then sat down and began to rebuild it. Al-Suddi said: rather, he plastered it, and began to build the wall.

﴿Musa said﴾: ﴿If you had wished, you could have taken a wage for it﴾. Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub read *latakhadhta* with a light ta and a kasra on the kha. The others read *lattakhadhta* with a doubled ta and a fatha on the kha. Both are dialects, like *ittaba'a* and *tabi'a*. ﴿For it﴾, meaning for repairing the wall; ﴿a wage﴾, meaning a reward. The meaning is: "You know that we are hungry, and that the people of the town did not feed us, so if you had taken a payment for your work."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verses 79–80:

﴿As for the boat, it belonged to poor men who worked on the sea.﴾ Ka'b said: It belonged to ten brothers, five of whom were chronically ill [[i.e., afflicted with a long-lasting illness. One says (zamina) the person (zamanan) and (zamanah), so he is (zamin), from the pattern of (ta'iba), and it is an illness that lasts a long time. The plural is (zamna), like (marda), "sick."]], and five of whom worked on the sea. In this there is evidence that a poor man (miskin), even if he owns something, does not lose the designation of poverty (maskanah) if what he owns does not suffice for his needs. ﴿Who worked on the sea﴾: that is, they hired out the boat and earned their living by it. ﴿So I wanted to damage it﴾: I would make it defective.

﴿And behind them﴾: that is, in front of them ﴿was a king﴾, as in His saying: "Behind him is Hell" [Ibrahim: 16].

It was also said: "behind them" means behind them, and their return on their journey passed by him. The first view is more correct, and it is supported by the reading of Ibn 'Abbas: "and there was in front of them a king" [[See: al-Tabari, 16/1–2; Zad al-Masir, 5/178.]].

﴿Who seized every boat by force﴾: that is, every sound boat by force. Ibn 'Abbas used to read it this way. So al-Khidr damaged it and made it defective, so that the seizing king would not take it. His name was al-Jalandi, and he was an unbeliever.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: His name was "Mutawallih ibn Jalandi al-Azdi."

Shu'ayb al-Jubba'i said: His name was "Hudad ibn Budad" [[See: al-Bukhari, Tafsir (exegesis) of Surat al-Kahf: 8/421.]].

It is related that al-Khidr apologized to the people and told them about the matter of the seizing king, and they did not know his news. He said: "I wanted, when it passed by him, that he would leave it because of its defect [[See: al-Bukhari, Tafsir of Surat al-Kahf: 8/421.]], and then when he had passed it, they would repair it and benefit from it." It was said: they sealed it with a piece of glass, and it was said: with pitch.

His, the Mighty and Majestic's, saying: ﴿As for the boy, his parents were believers, so we feared﴾: that is, we knew [[What is between the brackets is omitted in manuscript "B".]] ﴿that he would overburden them﴾: that is, overwhelm them. Al-Kalbi said: he would burden them ﴿with rebellion and disbelief﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "We feared that his love would lead them to follow him in his religion."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verses 81–82:

﴿So We intended that their Lord would replace them with one better than him in purity and nearer in mercy.﴾ Abu Ja'far, Nafi' and Abu 'Amr recited it with the doubled letter (tashdid) here, and in Surat al-Tahrim and Surat al-Qalam. The others recited it without doubling (takhfif), and both are dialects (lughatan). Some scholars distinguished between them, saying: "al-tabdil" (substitution) is changing a thing or changing its state while the substance of the thing remains, whereas "al-ibdal" (replacement) is removing a thing and putting another in its place. ﴿Their Lord would give them in exchange one better than him in purity﴾, meaning in righteousness and piety, ﴿and nearer in mercy﴾. Ibn 'Amir, Abu Ja'far and Ya'qub recited "ruhman" with a damma on the ha', while the rest recited it with a sukun (ruhman), meaning compassion (atfan min al-rahmah). It was also said that it derives from kinship (al-rahim wa al-qarabah). Qatadah said: that is, more joined to the ties of kinship and more dutiful to their parents. [Al-Tabari said: (16/4) "There is no sense of kinship (rahim) in this context, because the one who was killed, from whom his parents were replaced, was a child of his two parents, so their closeness to the parents and their nearness in kinship are the same."]

Al-Kalbi said: Allah replaced them with a female slave, whom a prophet of the prophets married, and she bore him a prophet, through whom Allah guided a nation of the nations.

And from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, who said: Allah replaced them with a female slave who bore seventy prophets. [Ibn 'Atiyyah said: This is far-fetched; the multitude of prophets is only known among the Children of Israel, and this woman was not one of them. (al-Bahr al-Muhit: 6/155).]

Ibn Juraij said: He replaced them with a boy. [See these sayings in al-Tabari: 16/3–4, Zad al-Masir: 5/180; al-Tabari inclined to the view that the meaning of the verse is that Allah replaced the boy for them with a girl.]

Mutarrif said: His parents rejoiced in him when he was born, and grieved over him when he was killed. Had he lived, it would have been their ruin. So let a person be content with the decree of Allah the Exalted, for Allah's decree for the believer in what he dislikes is better for him than His decree in what he loves.

The words of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city﴾, and their names were Asram and Sarim. ﴿And beneath it was a treasure belonging to them.﴾ They differed about that treasure. It was narrated from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "It was gold and silver." [Related by al-Tirmidhi in the commentary of Surat al-Kahf: 8/600, and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 2/369; it was also related by al-Bukhari in his History and by al-Tabarani (Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi: 8/601). Yazid ibn Yusuf al-San'ani is weak; al-Dhahabi said: "matruk" (abandoned), though his narration resembles the meaning of "treasure".]

'Ikrimah said: It was wealth.

And from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: The treasure was scrolls containing knowledge. [Related by al-Hakim, who authenticated it, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas: 2/369.]

And from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: It was a tablet of gold, inscribed with: "Wonder at one who is certain of death, how can he rejoice! Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 83:

His words, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿They ask you about Dhu al-Qarnayn. Say: I will recite to you a mention of him﴾. [It is] a report. They differed concerning his prophethood. Some of them said: he was a prophet. [[Said by Abdullah ibn Amr and al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim. See: Zad al-Masir: 5/184; al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 2/103.]]

[Abu al-Tufayl said: Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) was asked about Dhu al-Qarnayn, whether he was a prophet] [[What is between the brackets is omitted from "B".]] or a king? He said: "He was neither a prophet nor a king, but he was a servant who loved Allah and whom Allah loved; he gave sincere counsel to Allah, so Allah gave him sincere counsel." [[See: al-Tabari: 16/8.]]

It is also narrated that Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) heard a man say to another: "O Dhu al-Qarnayn!" He said: "You have named yourselves after the names of the prophets, and you were not content until you named yourselves after the names of the angels." [[Mentioned by al-Suhayli from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him). Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir said: it is gharib (strange). See: al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 2/103. Similar was mentioned by al-Qurtubi from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him): 11/46.]]

The majority hold that he was a just and righteous king. [[This is narrated from Ibn Abbas; al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir also preferred it, and al-Tabari narrated it from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him).]]

They differed concerning the reason for his being called "Dhu al-Qarnayn" (the Two-Horned). Al-Zuhri said: "Because he reached the two horns of the sun, its rising place and its setting place."

It was also said: "Because he ruled the Romans and the Persians."

It was also said: "Because he entered the light and the darkness."

It was also said: "Because he saw in a dream as if he took hold of the two horns of the sun."

It was also said: "Because he had two fine locks of hair."

It was also said: "Because he had two horns which his turban concealed."

Abu al-Tufayl narrated from Ali that he [said: he was called "Dhu al-Qarnayn" because] [[Addition from manuscript "B".]] he commanded his people to fear Allah, so they struck him on his right horn and he died; then Allah raised him up. Then he commanded them to fear Allah, so they struck him on his left horn and he died, and Allah revived him. [[See these sayings and others concerning his naming: al-Tabari: 16/8-9; Zad al-Masir: 5/183-184; al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/436 onward; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/47-48; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/102; al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 2/103.]]

They differed concerning his name. It was said: his name was "Marzuban ibn Mirzabbah al-Yunani," of the descendants of Yunan ibn Yafith ibn Nuh. It was also said: his name was "al-Iskandar ibn Filafus ibn Yamalus [[In "B": al-Iskandar ibn Qaylis ibn Filus al-Rumi.]] al-Rumi." [[See these with other sayings in: Zad al-Masir 5/183; al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 2/104-105. Moreover, neither these sayings nor the preceding ones are supported by any sound report from the Infallible ﷺ.]]

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Indeed, We established him in the land﴾: "made him dwell" (awtana). And *tamkin* (establishment) is the preparation of the means (*tamhid al-asbab*).

Ali said: He subjected the clouds to him, so he rode upon them, extended the means for him, and spread light for him, so that night and day were alike to him. This is the meaning of His establishing him in the land: He made travel through it easy for him and made its roads smooth for him.

﴿And We gave him of everything﴾ means: We gave him of everything that creatures need.

It was said: of everything that kings rely on to conquer cities and fight enemies.

﴿A means﴾ means: knowledge by which he attains whatever he wants, and by which he travels through the regions of the earth. *Sabab* is that which connects one thing to another.

Al-Hasan said: a means of reaching wherever he wished. It was said: We brought the regions of the earth near to him.

[[Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir (3/102): "...Thus was Dhu al-Qarnayn: God made the means easy for him, that is, the paths and the ways to conquer the regions, the districts, the cities and the lands, to break the enemies, to subdue the kings of the earth and to humiliate the people of polytheism. He was given of everything that one needs a means to, a means. And God knows best."]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verses 85–86:**

﴿So he followed a course﴾ — i.e., he took a path and proceeded. The people of the Hijaz and Basra recited "fa-ittaba'a" and "thumma ittaba'a" with a connected alif and a doubled ta' (ittaba'a). The others recited with a hamzated alif (atba'a) and a sukun on the ta'. It was said: their meaning is one.

The correct view is that there is a distinction between them. Whoever recites with the hamzated alif means: he reached and overtook. Whoever recites with the doubled ta' means: he traveled. It is said: "I kept following him (atba'uhu) until I caught up with him (atba'tuhu)," i.e., I kept traveling behind him until I overtook him.

As for His words ﴿a course﴾, i.e., a way. Ibn 'Abbas said: a station (manzilan).

﴿Until, when he reached the setting-place of the sun, he found it setting in a spring of murky water﴾. Abu Ja'far, Abu 'Amir, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr recited "hamiyah" with an unhamzated alif, meaning: hot. The others recited ﴿hami'atin﴾ with a hamza and without the alif, meaning: possessing murk (hama'ah), which is black mud.

Mu'awiyah asked Ka'b: "How do you find in the Torah that the sun sets?" He said: "We find in the Torah that it sets in water and mud."

al-Qutaybi said: it is possible that the meaning of His words ﴿in a spring of murky water﴾ is: near it there was a murky spring, or in the eye of the beholder.

﴿And he found near it a people﴾, i.e., near the spring, a nation. Ibn Jurayj said: a city with twelve thousand gates; had it not been for the clamour of its people, the splashing of the sun as it sets would have been heard.

﴿We said: O Dhu'l-Qarnayn﴾. Whoever claims that he was a prophet relies on this, since God Most High addressed him. The more correct view is that he was not a prophet, and what is meant is inspiration.

﴿Either you punish﴾, i.e., either you kill them if they do not enter Islam, ﴿or you take them with kindness﴾, i.e., you pardon and overlook. It was said: you capture them and teach them guidance. God gave him the choice between the two matters.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verses 87–90:

﴿He said: As for him who does wrong﴾, i.e., disbelieves, ﴿we will punish him﴾, i.e., we will kill him, ﴿then he will be returned to his Lord﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿and He will punish him with a terrible punishment﴾, i.e., a dreadful one, meaning: with the Fire, and the Fire is more dreadful than [[Missing from manuscript "A".]] killing.

﴿And as for him who believes and does righteous deeds, he will have a reward, the best﴾. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Hafs and Ya'qub read ﴿jaza'an﴾ (reward) in the accusative with tanwin, meaning: then for him is ﴿al-husna﴾ (the best), "jaza'an" being in the accusative as a masdar (verbal noun) that stands in the place of the hal (circumstantial accusative), i.e., for him is al-husna, being recompensed with it [[Missing from manuscript "B".]].

The others read it in the nominative, as an idafah (construct phrase), so al-husna is Paradise, and the reward is attributed to it, as He said: ﴿and the Hereafter's abode is better﴾ [Yusuf: 9], and "the abode" is the Hereafter.

It has also been said that what is meant by "al-husna" in this reading is the righteous deeds, i.e., for him is the reward of righteous deeds.

﴿And we will speak to him of Our command with ease﴾, i.e., we will speak gently to him and deal with him with ease from Our command. Mujahid said: "yusran" means "kindly" (ma'ruf).

﴿Then he followed a way﴾, i.e., he traveled routes and stages. [222/b] ﴿Until, when he reached the rising place of the sun﴾, i.e., the place where it rises, ﴿he found it rising over a people for whom We had made no screen against it﴾.
