Al-Baghawi's commentary (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verses 91–94:

His Exalted Majesty's saying: ﴿Thus﴾. It was said: its meaning is, just as he reached the place of the sun's setting, so he reached the place of its rising. The sound view is that its meaning is: just as He judged concerning the people who were at the sun's setting, so He judged concerning those who were at the sun's rising. ﴿And We had full knowledge of what was with him﴾, meaning: of what was with him and in his company of soldiers, equipment and instruments. "Khubran" means knowledge.

﴿Then he followed a way﴾.

﴿Until, when he reached between the two barriers﴾. Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and Hafs recited ﴿al-saddayn﴾ [the two barriers]. The word "sadda" here, with a fatha on the sin, agrees with Hamzah and al-Kisa'i on "sadda". [The others recited it with a damma on the sin. In Ya-Sin, "sadda" with a fatha was recited by Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs.] The rest recited it with a damma. Some said: both are dialectal forms with the same meaning. Ikrimah said: whatever is the work of the sons of Adam is "al-sadd" with a fatha, and whatever is the work of God is "sudd" with a damma. Abu 'Amr also said this. It was said: "al-sadd" with a fatha is a verbal noun, and with a damma it is a noun. Here, the two are two mountains, between which Dhul-Qarnayn set a barrier against Gog and Magog and those beyond them.

﴿He found beside them a people﴾, meaning: in front of the two barriers.

﴿Who could barely understand any speech﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿yufqihuna﴾ with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the qaf, meaning they could not make others understand speech. The others recited it with a fatha on the ya' and the qaf, meaning they could not understand the speech of others. Ibn Abbas said: they did not understand anyone's speech, and people did not understand their speech.

﴿They said: O Dhul-Qarnayn﴾. If it is asked: how did they say that when they could not understand? It is answered: a translator spoke on their behalf. The evidence for this is the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "They could barely understand any speech; those who were beside them said: O Dhul-Qarnayn."

﴿Indeed, Gog and Magog﴾. Asim recited both with two hamzas [and likewise in al-Anbiya', "Futihat Ya'juju wa Ma'juj"]. The others recited them without hamza [in both surahs]. Both are dialectal forms. Their origin is from the "ajij" of fire, which is its light and sparks. They were compared to it because of their multitude and their strength.

It was also said: with the hamza, they derive from the intensity of the "ajij" of fire; without the hamza, they are two non-Arabic names, like Harut and Marut. They are descendants of Yafith son of Noah.

Al-Dahhak said: they are a generation of the Turks. Al-Suddi said: the Turks are a detachment of Gog and Magog, which went out, and Dhul-Qarnayn struck the barrier [so the rest of them remained outside it; all the Turks are from them]. From Qatadah: they are twenty-two tribes. Dhul-Qarnayn built the barrier against twenty-one tribes, and one tribe remained. They are the Turks, and they were named Turks because they were left outside.

The historians said: the sons of Noah were three: Sam, Ham and Yafith. Sam is the father of the Arabs, the non-Arabs and the Romans. Ham is the father of the Abyssinians, the Zanj and the Nubians. Yafith is the father of the Turks, the Khazars, the Slavs, and Gog and Magog. Ibn Abbas, in a narration from Ata', said: they are ten parts, and the children of Adam are all one part. It is narrated from Hudhayfah, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed Gog is a nation and Magog is a nation; each nation is four hundred thousand nations. No man among them dies until he sees a thousand males from his own loins, all of them carrying weapons, and they are from the offspring of Adam, travelling towards the ruin of the world." It was also said: they are three categories. One category is like the cedar, a tree in Syria, whose height is one hundred and twenty cubits into the sky. Another category is equal in width and length, one hundred and twenty cubits, and no mountain or iron can withstand them. Another category has one of them spreading one of his ears as a mattress and covering himself with the other. They do not pass by an elephant, a wild animal or a pig without eating it, and whoever among them dies, they eat him. Their vanguard is in Syria and their rearguard is in Khurasan. They drink the rivers of the East and the Lake of Tiberias. [Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur (5/457) from Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn 'Adi, Ibn 'Asakir and Ibn al-Najjar.]

It is narrated from Ali that he said: among them is one whose height is a span, and among them is one who is excessively tall.

Ka'b said: they are an anomaly among the children of Adam. That is because Adam had a wet dream one day, and his semen mixed with the dust, so God created Gog and Magog from that water. They are connected to us through the father, not the mother. [Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir said (3/104–105): al-Nawawi, may God have mercy on him, in his Sharh Muslim, related from some people that Gog and Magog were created from the semen that came out of Adam and mixed with the dust, and so were created from that. On this view they would be created from Adam and not from Adam and Eve. This is a very strange view, and there is no evidence for it, neither from reason nor from transmission. One may not rely here on what some of the People of the Book relate, because of the fabricated traditions they have. And God knows best.]

Wahb ibn Munabbih mentioned: Dhul-Qarnayn was a man from the Romans, the son of an old woman. When he grew up, he was a righteous servant. God said to him: "I am sending you to nations of different tongues. Among them are two nations with the length of the earth between them: one of them at the sun's setting, called Nasik, and the other at its rising, called Mansak. And two nations with the width of the earth between them: one in the right quarter of the earth, called Hawil, and the other in the left quarter of the earth, called Tawil. And nations in the middle of the earth, among them jinn, humans, Gog and Magog." Dhul-Qarnayn said: "With what strength shall I overpower them? With what multitude shall I outnumber them? With what tongue shall I speak to them?" God, Mighty and Majestic, said: "I will make your path easy, I will loosen your tongue, I will strengthen your arm. Let nothing terrify you, and I will clothe you with awe so nothing will startle you. I will make light and darkness subject to you and make them among your soldiers. The light will guide you from in front of you, and the darkness will surround you from behind you."

So he set out until he reached the place of the sun's setting, and he found a multitude and a number that no one could count but God. He overpowered them with the darkness until he gathered them in one place, and he called them to God and to worshipping Him. Some of them believed and some turned away from him. He turned to those who turned away from him, and brought the darkness upon them, so it entered their bodies and their houses. Then they entered into his call. He mustered from the people of the west a great army, and he set out leading them while the darkness drove them, until he reached Hawil. He acted among them as he had acted in Nasik. Then he passed on until he reached Mansak at the sun's rising, and he acted there and mustered from it troops, as he had acted in the two nations. Then he took the left side of the earth and came to Tawil, and acted there as he had acted before. Then he turned to the nations in the middle of the earth. When he approached the part near the end of the Turks towards the East, a righteous nation of humans said to him: "O Dhul-Qarnayn, between these two mountains are creatures resembling beasts. They prey on animals and wild beasts, [they have fangs and molars] like predators. They eat snakes, scorpions, and every living creature created on the earth, and no creation increases as their increase does. Without doubt, they will fill the earth, overcome us and corrupt it. So shall we give you a tribute on condition that you place a barrier between us and them?" He said: "What my Lord has established me in is better. Bring me blocks of rock, iron and copper, until I know their measure."

So he set out until he reached the middle of their lands, and he found them of one size. The height of each of them was like half of a man of medium stature among us. They had claws like our fingernails, fangs and molars like predators, and they had a covering of hair on their bodies that shielded them and protected them from heat and cold. Each of them had two huge ears: one he spread as a mattress and with the other he covered himself. In summer he lives in one and in winter in the other. They copulate like beasts wherever they meet. When Dhul-Qarnayn saw this, he turned to the area between the two cliffs. He measured the distance between them and dug the foundation until he reached the water. He filled its inside with rock, and its mortar was copper poured in molten form. It became like a vein of a mountain beneath the earth. [Al-Tabari related it from Wahb ibn Munabbih, 16/17–21. Ibn Kathir commented on it in his tafsir (3/105): Ibn Jarir mentioned here a lengthy, strange and wondrous report about the journey of Dhul-Qarnayn, his building of the barrier and how events happened to him. In it there is length, strangeness and oddity, regarding their forms, their characteristics, their height, the shortness of some of them, and their ears. Ibn Abi Hatim related strange traditions about this from his father, whose chains are not sound. And God knows best.]

God, Exalted, said: ﴿They said: O Dhul-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog are corrupters in the land﴾. Al-Kalbi said: their corruption was that in the spring they would go out to their land and leave nothing green that they did not eat, and nothing dry that they did not carry off and bring into their land. They inflicted great harm and killing upon the people.

It was also said: their corruption was that they ate people.

It was also said: the meaning is that they will corrupt the land when they come out. [Al-Tabari preferred this view, 16/22.]

﴿So shall we pay you a tribute﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited "kharajan" with an alif, "kharaj". The others recited ﴿kharjan﴾ without an alif. Both are dialectal forms with the same meaning: a reward and wage from our wealth.

Abu 'Amr said: "al-kharj" is what you give voluntarily, and "al-kharaj" is what it is obligatory for you to pay. It was also said: "al-kharaj" is on land, and "al-kharj" is on persons. One says: pay the head-tax of your head and the land-tax of your city.

﴿On condition that you place between us and them a barrier﴾, meaning: a barrier so that they cannot reach us.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verses 96–98 (part 1 of 2):**

﴿Give me﴾: i.e., bring me. Abu Bakr read it as "Ītūnī," meaning "bring to me." ﴿Blocks of iron﴾: i.e., pieces of iron; its singular is zubrah. So they brought them to him, along with the firewood, and he placed some of them upon others. He continued placing the iron upon the firewood and the firewood upon the iron ﴿until, when he had made level between the two cliffs﴾. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub read it with a ḍammah on the ṣād and the dāl; Abu Bakr read the dāl with a sukun; the others read both with a fatḥah. They are the two mountains. Sawa (made level): i.e., he leveled the two sides of the two mountains.

﴿He said: Blow﴾. In the narrative: he placed the coal and the firewood among the blocks of iron, then said: "Blow," meaning: into the fire.

﴿Until, when he had made it fire﴾: i.e., the iron became fire. ﴿He said: Bring me﴾. Hamzah and Abu Bakr read it with wasl (connected alif); the others read it with a hamzah (qat' al-alif).

﴿I will pour over it molten copper﴾: i.e., [bring me copper, I will pour over it]. "Al-ifragh" means pouring, and "al-qitr" is melted copper. The fire then consumed the firewood, and the copper took the place of the firewood, until the iron adhered to the copper.

Qatadah said: it was like striped cloth, with a black stripe and a red stripe. In the narrative: its width was fifty cubits, its height two hundred cubits, and its length a farsakh.

﴿So they were unable to scale it﴾: i.e., to climb over it from above, because of its height and smoothness. ﴿Nor could they make a hole in it﴾: from below, because of its strength and hardness. Hamzah read ﴿fa-mā stāṭa'ū﴾ with a shaddah on the ṭā', assimilating the tā' of the ifti'al form into the ṭā'.

﴿He said﴾: meaning Dhu al-Qarnayn. ﴿This﴾: i.e., the barrier. ﴿Is a mercy﴾: i.e., a blessing ﴿from my Lord. So when the promise of my Lord comes﴾: it was said: the Day of Resurrection, and it was said: the time of their emergence. ﴿He will make it level (dakkā')﴾. The people of Kufa read ﴿dakkā'﴾ with a long vowel and a hamzah, meaning: a smooth ground. The others read it without the long vowel, meaning: made flattened and level with the surface of the earth. ﴿And the promise of my Lord is ever true﴾.

Qatadah narrated from Abu Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, who raised it (to the Prophet ﷺ): "Indeed Ya'juj and Ma'juj dig into it every day, until, when they nearly see the rays of the sun, the one in charge of them says: Return, for you will dig it tomorrow. Then Allah restores it as it was, until, when their term is fulfilled, they dig until, when they nearly see the rays of the sun, the one in charge of them says: Return, for you will dig it tomorrow, if Allah wills, and he makes an exception. They return to it, and it is in the state in which they left it, so they dig it through and come out upon the people, and they pursue the waters, and the people fortify themselves in their fortresses against them. They shoot their arrows toward the sky, and the arrows return to them like blood, and they say: We have subdued the people of the earth and overcome the people of the heaven. Then Allah sends upon them a worm in their necks (nagaf), and they perish. The beasts of the earth grow fat and are nourished (tashkuru) on their flesh, nourished abundantly."

[Footnotes from the original as translated: Al-Tirmidhi in al-Tafsir (8/597–599), who said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith; we only know it from this route"; Ibn Majah in al-Fitan, no. 4080 (2/1364–1365); Ibn Hibban (no. 470 in Mawarid al-Zam'an), authenticated by al-Hakim on the conditions of the two Shaykhs (4/488); Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad (2/510). Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (3/106): "Its isnad is good and strong, but its raised text is strange, for the apparent meaning of the verse requires that they were unable to climb it or to pierce it because of its firm construction, strength and hardness. But this has been transmitted from Ka'b al-Ahbar: that before their emergence they come to it and lick it until only a little remains of it, and they say: Tomorrow we will open it. [Footnote: "yadān" is the dual of yad, meaning no power or ability; "fa-ḥarriz" means gather them and make them a refuge for them.] "Allah sends forth Ya'juj and Ma'juj, who swarm from every slope. The first of them pass by the lake of Tiberias and drink all that is in it, and the last of them pass and say: There was once water here. The prophet of Allah and his companions are besieged until the head of an ox is better for one of them than a hundred dinars is for any of you today. The prophet of Allah Isa and his companions beseech Allah, so Allah sends upon them the worm in their necks, and they wake up dead like one soul. Then the prophet of Allah Isa and his companions descend to the earth, and they find no place a hand's breadth free except that it is filled with their fat and stench. The prophet of Allah Isa and his companions beseech Allah, so Allah sends birds like the necks of Bukht camels, which carry them and cast them where Allah wills. Then Allah sends a rain that no house of clay or wool can shelter from, and it washes the earth until it leaves it like a smooth pool. Then it is said to the earth: Bring forth your fruit and return your blessing. On that day a band will eat from a pomegranate and shelter under its husk, and milk will be blessed, so that a single milch camel suffices a multitude, a milch cow suffices a tribe, and a milch goat suffices a clan. While they are thus, Allah sends a pleasant wind that takes them under their armpits and seizes the soul of every believer and every Muslim, and there remain the wicked of mankind who copulate openly like donkeys, and upon them the Hour will come." [Footnotes: Muslim, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 2137 (4/2250–2255).]

Similarly, Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj related to us: Ali ibn Hujr al-Sa'di related to us: Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir and al-Walid ibn Muslim ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir related to us with this isnad, similar to what we mentioned, and he added after his saying "there was once water here": "Then they proceed until they reach Mount al-Khamr [footnote: in A: 'Ahmar', in B: 'al-Hamr' with unpointed ḥā', and the affirmed reading is from Sahih Muslim; al-khamr is the dense shrubbery that conceals whoever is in it; the hadith explains that it is the mountain of Bayt al-Maqdis because of its many trees], which is the mountain of Bayt al-Maqdis. They say: We have destroyed those on the earth; come, let us kill those in the heaven. So they shoot their arrows (nushshab) toward the sky, and Allah returns their arrows to them stained with blood." [Footnote: Muslim, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 2137 (4/2255).]

Wahb said: They used to come to the sea and drink its water and eat its creatures, then they would eat wood and trees, and whatever people they could seize. They could not reach Makkah, nor Madinah, nor Bayt al-Maqdis.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 96–98 (part 2 of 2):

Abdul-Wahid al-Maliḥī informed us: Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymī informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Ahmad informed us: my father informed us: Ibrahim informed us, from al-Hajjaj ibn Hajjaj, from Qatadah, from Abdullah ibn Abi Utbah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The House will certainly be visited for Hajj and 'Umrah after the emergence of Ya'juj and Ma'juj" [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Hajj, chapter on the words of Allah, "Allah made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a means of standing for mankind": 3/454, and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/83.]

And in the narrative: Dhu al-Qarnayn entered the darkness, and when he returned, he died in Shahrazur. Some of them mentioned that his age was a little over thirty years.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 99–102:

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿And We will leave them that day surging over one another﴾. It is said: this is at the opening of the barrier. He says: We will leave Gog and Magog surging, i.e., some of them will enter upon others like the surging of water, and some of them will mix with others because of their great numbers.

It is also said: this is at the establishment of the Hour, when creation will enter upon one another and their humans will mix with their jinn, bewildered.

﴿And the Horn will be blown﴾, because the emergence of Gog and Magog is one of the signs of the nearness of the Hour. ﴿Then We will gather them in a [single] gathering﴾ into one plain.

﴿And We will present﴾, i.e., We will make manifest, ﴿Hell that day to the disbelievers, in presentation﴾, until they witness it directly.

﴿Those whose eyes were in a covering﴾, i.e., a veil, and "the covering" is that by which a thing is covered and concealed, ﴿from My remembrance﴾, meaning: from faith and the Qur'an, and from guidance and clarification. It is also said: from seeing the signs.

﴿And they were not able to hear﴾, i.e., the hearing of acceptance and faith, due to the dominance of wretchedness over them.

It is also said: they did not understand. It is also said: they were not able, i.e., they were not able to hear from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what he recited to them, because of their intense enmity toward him, like the saying of a man: "I cannot hear anything from so-and-so because of his enmity."

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿Then do those who disbelieve think﴾, i.e., suppose, ﴿that they may take My servants as allies instead of Me?﴾ — lords. By "servants" He means ʿIsa and the angels. ﴿No! Rather, they will be enemies to them and will disown them.﴾

Ibn ʿAbbas said: it means the devils whom they obeyed instead of Allah. Muqatil said: the idols were called "servants," as He said: ﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah are servants like you﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 194]. The answer to this interrogative is omitted.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: it means: I am indeed jealous for Myself. He says: Do those who disbelieve suppose that they may take others besides Me as allies, and that I will not be jealous for Myself nor punish them?

It is also said: did they suppose that taking My servants as allies instead of Me would benefit them?

﴿Indeed, We have prepared Hell for the disbelievers as a welcome [nuzul]﴾, i.e., a dwelling place. Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is their abode. It is also said: the nuzul is what is prepared for a guest; meaning, it is made ready for them with Us, like a welcome for a guest.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verses 103–105:

﴿Say, "Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?"﴾ That is: those who exhausted themselves in an action through which they hoped for favour and reward, and so they gained destruction and ruin. They are like one who buys a commodity, hoping for profit from it, but he suffers loss and his effort is in vain.

The scholars differed concerning them. Ibn 'Abbas and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas said: they are the Jews and the Christians. It was also said: they are the monks.

﴿Those﴾ who confined themselves in the monasteries. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: they are the people of Harurah [[The meaning of this from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) is that this noble verse includes the Harurites (Kharijites) as it includes the Jews, the Christians and others, not that it was revealed specifically concerning these people nor those, but it is more general than this. This verse is Meccan, before the address to the Jews and Christians and before the existence of the Kharijites at all. Rather, it is general to everyone who worships Allah in a way that is not pleasing, while thinking he is correct in it and that his deed is accepted, while he is mistaken and his deed is rejected, as Allah the Exalted said: "Faces that Day will be humbled, labouring and exhausted, burning in a scorching fire" [88:2–4], and Allah the Exalted said: "And We will regard the deeds they did and make them scattered dust" [25:23]. See: Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3 / 108. This is also what al-Tabari said, where he preferred that it refers to every doer of a deed that he thinks is correct, and that by doing it he is obedient to Allah and pleasing to Him, while by that deed he is displeasing to Allah and deviating from the way of the people of faith in Him, such as the monastics, the Shammasa and their likes among those who strive in their misguidance; and they, despite their deeds and striving, are disbelievers in Allah, from whatever religion they are. See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 16 / 34.]] ﴿Their effort went astray﴾ in the life of this world, their deed and striving became void, ﴿while they think they are doing well in work﴾, that is, in deed.

﴿Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and in meeting Him, so their deeds have become worthless﴾, that is, they have become void. ﴿So We will not assign for them on the Day of Resurrection any weight﴾, that is, We will not give them any importance or value. The Arabs say: "So-and-so has no weight with me," meaning he has no standing because of his lowliness.

'Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Ahmad related to us from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah related to us: Sa'id ibn Maryam related to us: al-Mughirah informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "A great, fat man will come on the Day of Resurrection, and he will not weigh a wing of a mosquito with Allah." Then he said, "Recite if you wish: ﴿So We will not assign for them on the Day of Resurrection any weight﴾" [[Reported by al-Bukhari in the Book of Tafsir, chapter "Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and in meeting Him...": 8 / 426, and Muslim in the Book of the Attributes of the Hypocrites and their Rulings, chapter on the description of the Resurrection, Paradise and Hell, no. (2785): 4 / 2147.]].

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: People will come on the Day of Resurrection with deeds which, in their own estimation, are as great as the mountains of Tihamah. But when they are weighed, they will weigh nothing. That is the meaning of His the Exalted's saying: ﴿So We will not assign for them on the Day of Resurrection any weight﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 18, verse 108–110:

﴿Abiding therein forever; they will not desire any removal from it.﴾ "They will not seek" (لَا يَبْغُونَ). "Removal from it" (عَنْهَا حِوَلًا) means a transfer to something else. Ibn ʿAbbas said: they will not wish to move away from it, as a man moves from a house that does not suit him to another house.

His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as a supplement.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: The Jews said, "O Muhammad [[Omitted from "B".]], you claim that we have been given wisdom, and in your Book, 'He who is given wisdom has been given much good,' and then you say, 'And you have been given only a little knowledge'?" So Allah revealed this verse [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. 346; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/68; al-Bahr al-Muhit: 6/168; Tafsir al-Khazin: 4/192.]].

It is also said: when "And you have been given only a little knowledge" was revealed, the Jews said, "We have been given the Torah, and in it is the knowledge of everything," and then Allah the Exalted revealed [[See: Zad al-Masir: 5/201.]] ﴿Say: If the sea were ink...﴾. The ink is called midad because it supplies (imdad) the scribe; its root meaning is increase and one thing coming after another.

Mujahid said: "If the sea were ink for the pen, and the pen were writing, ﴿the sea would be exhausted﴾," meaning its water, ﴿before the words of my Lord were exhausted﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "yanfada" with the yā' (because the verb is placed before its subject), while the rest read it with the tā'. ﴿The words of my Lord﴾ means His knowledge and His decree. ﴿And if We brought the like of it as a supplement﴾ means: even if all creatures were writing and the sea were supplying them, the sea would be exhausted and the words of my Lord would not be exhausted; and even if We brought the like of the sea's water in its abundance as a supplement or addition. ["Madadan" is in the accusative as a specification (tamyiz).] Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens, and the sea, with seven more seas added to it, were ink, the words of Allah would not be exhausted﴾ [Luqman: 27].

His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Say: I am only a human being like you; it is revealed to me that your God is one God.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: Allah taught His Messenger humility, lest he become arrogant toward His creation, so He commanded him to acknowledge and say: "I am a human being like you, except that I have been singled out with revelation, and Allah has honored me with it: it is revealed to me that your God is one God, having no partner." ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord﴾ means fears the return to Him. It is also said: he hopes to see his Lord. Thus "hope" (al-raja') can mean both fear and expectation. The poet said: "Not everything you hope for of good will come to be, nor will everything you hope for of evil necessarily befall you." So he combined both meanings.

﴿Let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord.﴾ That is: let him not show off with his deeds.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us; Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Abu Nuʿaym informed us; Sufyan informed us, from Salamah, that is Ibn Kuhayl, who said: I heard Jundub say: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever makes his deed heard [for show], Allah will make it heard [expose him]; and whoever shows off, Allah will make a show of him." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Riqaq, chapter on riya' and sum'ah: 11/335-336, and Muslim in al-Birr wa'l-Silah, chapter on praise of the righteous being good tidings that do not harm him, no. 2642: 4/2034-2035; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/323.]]

And it has been transmitted to us from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "The thing I fear most for you is the minor shirk," and they said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is the minor shirk?" He said: "Showing off (riya')." [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad: 5/428-429. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/324. Al-Haythami said, "its men are the men of the Sahih," and al-Mundhiri said, "its chain is good." It was also transmitted by Ibn Abi al-Dunya, al-Bayhaqi in al-Zuhd, and others. Mahmud ibn Labid saw the Prophet ﷺ but, as I see it, his hearing from him is not authentically established. Abu Bakr ibn Khuzaymah included the hadith of Mahmud mentioned above in his Sahih, though he does not include any mursal reports in it. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned that al-Bukhari said he had companionship (suhbah), and that his father said it is not known that he had companionship. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr preferred that he had companionship. Al-Tabarani transmitted it with a good chain from Mahmud ibn Labid from Rafi' ibn Khadij, and it has been said that the hadith of Mahmud is correct without the mention of Rafi' in it, and Allah knows best. See: al-Targhib wa'l-Tarhib: 1/69; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 1/102; and compare: al-Nahj al-Sadid fi Takhrij Ahadith Taysir al-Aziz al-Hamid, p. 46.]]

Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Salihi informed us; Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn Musa al-Sayrafi informed us; Abu'l-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Asamm informed us; Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam informed us; my father informed us; Shu'ayb informed us, who said: al-Layth informed us, from Abu'l-Hadi, from Amr, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: I am the most independent of partners in regard to association. Whoever does a deed in which he associates others with Me, I am free of it, and it is for the one who did it." [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Zuhd wa'l-Raqa'iq, chapter on one who associates others with Allah in his deed, no. 2985: 4/2289, with the wording "...I leave him and his shirk." Ibn Majah narrated it in al-Zuhd, chapter on riya' and sum'ah, no. 4202: 2/1405, and said in the Zawa'id: "its chain is sahih." The author narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/325. See also: al-Targhib wa'l-Tarhib: 1/69, and consult Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/109-111, for he cites a number of hadiths on riya'.]]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us; Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us; Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Rayyani informed us; Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us; Hafs ibn Umar informed us; Hammam informed us, from Qatadah; Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd al-Ghatafani informed us, from Ma'dan ibn Abi Talhah, from Abu'l-Darda', who narrated it from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever memorizes ten verses from the beginning of Surah al-Kahf will be protected from the trial of the Dajjal." [[Narrated by Muslim in Salat al-Musafirin, chapter on the virtue of Surah al-Kahf and Ayat al-Kursi, no. 809: 1/555. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/469.]]

And Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us; Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani informed us; Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani informed us; Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us; Abu'l-Aswad informed us; Ibn Lahi'ah informed us, from Ziyad, from Sahl, that is Ibn Mu'adh, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever recites the beginning and the end of Surah al-Kahf, it will be a light for him from his feet up to his head; and whoever recites it entirely, it will be a light for him from the earth to the sky." [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 3/439. Al-Haythami said, "Ahmad and al-Tabarani narrated it, and in its chain is Ibn Lahi'ah, who is weak, though his hadith may be considered good." See: Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/52. The author narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/469-470.]] [[At the end of the Makkah Haram library copy: "The first volume of the Tafsir of al-Baghawi is completed by the praise and help of Allah, and its completion was at the Noble Sanctuary (Jerusalem), in the Salahiyyah Madrasah, may Allah keep it, on the thirteenth of Shawwal of the year 825 AH. Its scribe, the humble servant in need of Allah, the Self-Sufficient: Sulayman ibn Ahmad ibn Ahmad ibn Sulayman al-Haddadi al-Qurashi, praising Allah the Exalted and invoking blessings upon His Prophet Muhammad, his family, companions and wives. Followed by the second half; the beginning of Surah Maryam. May Allah forgive him, his parents, and all the Muslims. Amin." Then follows a line recording ownership of the copy by one hoping for his Lord's pardon and forgiveness: Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Hariri, may Allah pardon him.]]

Ibn Majah narrated it in al-Zuhd, chapter on riya' and sum'ah, no. 4202: 2/1405, and said in the Zawa'id: "its chain is sahih." The author narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/325. See also: al-Targhib wa'l-Tarhib: 1/69, and consult Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/109-111, for he cites a number of hadiths on riya'.]]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us; Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us; Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Rayyani informed us; Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us; Hafs ibn Umar informed us; Hammam informed us, from Qatadah; Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd al-Ghatafani informed us, from Ma'dan ibn Abi Talhah, from Abu'l-Darda', who narrated it from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever memorizes ten verses from the beginning of Surah al-Kahf will be protected from the trial of the Dajjal." [[Narrated by Muslim in Salat al-Musafirin, chapter on the virtue of Surah al-Kahf and Ayat al-Kursi, no. 809: 1/555. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/469.]]

And Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us; Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani informed us; Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani informed us; Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us; Abu'l-Aswad informed us; Ibn Lahi'ah informed us, from Ziyad, from Sahl, that is Ibn Mu'adh, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever recites the beginning and the end of Surah al-Kahf, it will be a light for him from his feet up to his head; and whoever recites it entirely, it will be a light for him from the earth to the sky." [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 3/439. Al-Haythami said, "Ahmad and al-Tabarani narrated it, and in its chain is Ibn Lahi'ah, who is weak, though his hadith may be considered good." See: Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/52. The author narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/469-470.]] [[At the end of the Makkah Haram library copy: "The first volume of the Tafsir of al-Baghawi is completed by the praise and help of Allah, and its completion was at the Noble Sanctuary (Jerusalem), in the Salahiyyah Madrasah, may Allah keep it, on the thirteenth of Shawwal of the year 825 AH. Its scribe, the humble servant in need of Allah, the Self-Sufficient: Sulayman ibn Ahmad ibn Ahmad ibn Sulayman al-Haddadi al-Qurashi, praising Allah the Exalted and invoking blessings upon His Prophet Muhammad, his family, companions and wives. Followed by the second half; the beginning of Surah Maryam. May Allah forgive him, his parents, and all the Muslims. Amin." Then follows a line recording ownership of the copy by one hoping for his Lord's pardon and forgiveness: Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Hariri, may Allah pardon him.]]
